Even if not committed, it's a bad practice that normalizes real keys in config files.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Immediately rotate the Sendbyte API key\n2. Remove the duplicate entry from `.env`\n3. Audit git history: `git log --all -p -- apps/api/.env`\n4. Add a pre-commit hook or gitleaks rule to block `sk_test_` or `sk_live_` patterns\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 2\n\n**TITLE:** `.env` file missing `QUOTE_SECRET`, `PAYCODE_SECRET`, and `ENCRYPTION_KEY` — server will panic on boot\n\n**SEVERITY:** Critical\n\n**CATEGORY:** DevOps / Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/.env` (entire file), `apps/api/internal/config/config.go` lines 68–85\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `.env` file (the one developers actually use) is missing `QUOTE_SECRET`, `PAYCODE_SECRET`, and `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. The `config.Load()` function calls `panic()` via `mustEnv()` for `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, and `JWT_SECRET`, and returns errors for the three missing keys. The server will fail to start in any environment where this `.env` is used as-is. The `.env.example` has these keys documented, but the actual `.env` does not.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe `.env` file appears to be an older version that predates the addition of these required secrets. The `.env.example` was updated but the actual `.env` was not synced.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nAny developer or deployment that uses this `.env` directly will get a boot failure. More critically, if someone copies `.env` to production without adding these keys, all package orders with recipient PII will fail, all QR paycodes will fail, and all quote signing will fail.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd the three missing keys to `.env`:\n```\nENCRYPTION_KEY=<generate: openssl rand -hex 16>\nPAYCODE_SECRET=<generate: openssl rand -hex 32>\nQUOTE_SECRET=<generate: openssl rand -hex 32>\n```\nAlso add `MONNIFY_WALLET_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` which is required in production.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 3\n\n**TITLE:** Driver bank account resolution not implemented — driver cashouts will always fail\n\n**SEVERITY:** Critical\n\n**CATEGORY:** Business / Backend\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/wallet.go`, `ResolveCashoutRecipient()`, last line\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\nreturn \"\", \"\", \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"driver bank account resolution not yet implemented\")\n```\nThe `ResolveCashoutRecipient` function explicitly returns an error for drivers. This means every driver EWA cashout and every weekly auto-payout will fail at the worker stage. The money is debited from the driver's wallet, the cashout record is created, but the actual bank transfer will always fail and trigger a reversal. Drivers will never receive money to their bank accounts.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe driver bank account model and resolution logic was not implemented. The merchant path was built but the driver path was left as a stub.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nDrivers cannot get paid. This is a complete business failure for the rider supply side. Drivers will churn immediately when they discover they can't cash out.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Add a `driver_bank_accounts` table (similar to `merchant_bank_accounts`)\n2. Add API endpoints for drivers to save/update their bank account\n3. Implement the driver resolution path in `ResolveCashoutRecipient`\n4. Add a driver bank account UI in the driver app\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 4\n\n**TITLE:** Merchant bank account name is user-supplied, not provider-verified\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security / Finance\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/handler/merchant.go` (SaveBankAccount), `apps/merchant/app/page.tsx` bank form\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `MerchantBankAccount` model has a comment: \"account_name is provider-resolved, not user-supplied.\" However, the merchant portal UI has a free-text `accountName` input field that the merchant fills in manually. There is no evidence in the codebase that the account name is actually verified against the payment provider's account resolution API before saving. The model's `IsVerified` field defaults to `true` without any actual verification step.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe model was designed with the intent to verify, but the verification step was not implemented in the handler or service layer.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nMerchants can enter any account name. Payouts could go to wrong accounts. In Nigeria, bank account name verification (via Paystack's `resolve_account` or Monnify's equivalent) is a standard fraud prevention step. Skipping it exposes the platform to misdirected payouts and social engineering.\n\n**FIX:**\nBefore saving a bank account, call the payment provider's account resolution API:\n- Paystack: `GET /bank/resolve?account_number=...&bank_code=...`\n- Monnify: `GET /api/v1/disbursements/account/validate`\n\nOnly save the provider-returned account name, never the user-supplied one. Return the resolved name to the UI for confirmation before saving.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 5\n\n**TITLE:** No customer support system — users have no recourse when orders fail\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Business / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** Entire codebase — feature absent\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThere is no in-app support flow for customers. No chat, no ticket system, no \"report a problem\" button, no dispute initiation from the customer side. The admin panel has dispute/escrow management, but customers have no way to trigger it. When a delivery goes wrong (wrong item, damaged goods, driver no-show, overcharge), the customer is stuck.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nSupport infrastructure was not built as part of the initial scope.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nIn the Nigerian market, trust is built through responsive support. Without it, the first bad experience will result in a negative social media post. Chargeback rates will be high because customers will dispute with their banks instead of the platform.\n\n**FIX:**\nAt minimum before launch:\n1. Add a \"Report a problem\" button on the order detail screen that opens a WhatsApp chat or email\n2. Add a support contact to the order receipt\n3. Document the dispute escalation process for the admin team\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes (business risk)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 6\n\n**TITLE:** OSRM defaults to public demo server in production — pricing and dispatch will fail under load\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** DevOps / Backend\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/config/config.go` line 57, `apps/api/.env`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `.env` file has `OSRM_URL=http://router.project-osrm.org`. The config correctly blocks this in production (`config.go` returns an error if `OSRM_URL` is the public demo in production). However, the `docker-compose.yml` OSRM container is a placeholder that just sleeps — it doesn't actually run OSRM. There is no evidence of a production OSRM deployment with Nigerian road data loaded.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nOSRM requires a large preprocessing step (downloading OSM data for Nigeria, running `osrm-extract`, `osrm-partition`, `osrm-customize`) that hasn't been completed.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nWithout a private OSRM instance with Nigerian road data, the server will refuse to start in production (config validation). Even if the public demo is used (by changing the config check), it has no Nigerian road data and will return incorrect distances, causing wrong pricing for every order.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Download Nigeria OSM data from Geofabrik\n2. Run OSRM preprocessing pipeline\n3. Deploy OSRM on Railway/Fly.io with a persistent volume\n4. Set `OSRM_URL` to the private instance in production\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 7\n\n**TITLE:** Rate limiter fails open on Redis errors — auth endpoints unprotected during Redis outage\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/middleware/ratelimit.go` lines 22–25\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\nif err != nil {\n    // fail open — don't block on Redis errors\n    c.Next()\n    return\n}\n```\nWhen Redis is unavailable, the rate limiter allows all requests through. This means during a Redis outage (or a targeted Redis DoS), the auth endpoints (`/auth/login`, `/otp/request`) become completely unprotected. An attacker who can disrupt Redis can then brute-force credentials or OTPs at unlimited rate.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nAvailability was prioritized over security for the rate limiter. This is a reasonable tradeoff for most endpoints but not for auth.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nDuring any Redis disruption, credential stuffing and OTP brute-force attacks become trivially possible.\n\n**FIX:**\nFor auth and OTP endpoints specifically, fail closed (return 503) rather than fail open when Redis is unavailable. For other endpoints, fail open is acceptable. Differentiate by passing a `failClosed bool` parameter to `RateLimit`.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 8\n\n**TITLE:** No PIN brute-force protection — wallet PIN can be guessed indefinitely\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/auth.go` `VerifyPIN()`, `apps/api/internal/service/paycode.go` `ConfirmByCard()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe PIN verification functions (`VerifyPIN`, `ConfirmByCard`) have no attempt counting, no lockout, and no rate limiting beyond the general wallet transfer rate limit (10/min). A 4-digit PIN has 10,000 combinations. At 10 attempts/minute, it can be brute-forced in ~17 hours. The `ConfirmByCard` path has no rate limiting at all — it's on the `/paycodes/scan-card` endpoint which has the general `paycodes` rate limit of 20/min, meaning a 4-digit PIN can be brute-forced in ~8 hours.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nPIN lockout was not implemented.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nAny attacker who obtains a customer's SpeedPlus card QR payload (e.g., by photographing it) can brute-force the PIN and drain the wallet.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Add a `pin_attempts` counter to the `pins` table\n2. Lock the PIN after 5 failed attempts, requiring OTP to unlock\n3. Add per-user rate limiting on PIN verification (not just per-IP)\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 9\n\n**TITLE:** Idempotency middleware uses `SetNX` without atomic read-then-set — race condition on concurrent identical requests\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Concurrency\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/middleware/idempotency.go` lines 55–70\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe idempotency middleware uses `SetNX` to claim a key. If `SetNX` returns `false` (key exists), it reads the cached response with a separate `GET`. Between the `SetNX` and the `GET`, the key could expire (if the first request failed and set a 2-minute error TTL that just expired) and a second concurrent request could claim it. This is a TOCTOU race. More practically: if the first request is still processing (sentinel value), the second request returns 409 \"in progress\" — which is correct — but if the first request fails and the key expires before the second request's `GET`, the second request will also get `SetNX=false` but then `GET` will return a nil/error, and the code falls through to return 409 \"in progress\" even though nothing is processing.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nRedis doesn't have a native atomic \"get-or-set-with-processing-sentinel\" operation without Lua scripting.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nUnder concurrent load with the same idempotency key, a small window exists where a second request could be incorrectly rejected as \"in progress\" when the first has already completed. For money-moving operations, this could cause a user to think their payment failed when it succeeded.\n\n**FIX:**\nUse a Lua script for atomic check-and-set, or use Redis `GETSET` / `SET NX GET` (Redis 7+) to atomically get the old value while setting the new one.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (low probability, but worth fixing)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 10\n\n**TITLE:** `WeeklyAutoPayout` ignores errors from `ListDriversWithUnpaidEarnings`\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Finance\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/wallet.go` line ~220\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\ndrivers, _ := s.repo.ListDriversWithUnpaidEarnings(ctx)\n```\nThe error is silently discarded. If the DB query fails, `drivers` is nil/empty and the entire weekly payout run silently processes zero drivers. No error is logged, no alert is fired.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nError handling was omitted.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nA DB error during the weekly payout cron will silently skip all driver payouts for that week. Drivers won't be paid. The error won't be visible until drivers complain.\n\n**FIX:**\n```go\ndrivers, err := s.repo.ListDriversWithUnpaidEarnings(ctx)\nif err != nil {\n    return fmt.Errorf(\"weekly payout: list drivers: %w\", err)\n}\n```\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (but high business impact)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 11\n\n**TITLE:** `ConfirmByCard` finds \"active in-transit order\" by customer — wrong order could be settled if customer has multiple concurrent orders\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/paycode.go` `ConfirmByCard()`, `apps/api/internal/repo/paycode.go` `FindActiveInTransitOrder()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe card-based delivery confirmation finds the customer's active in-transit order by `customer_id` alone. If a customer somehow has two in-transit orders (e.g., a subscription order and a manual order both dispatched simultaneously), the wrong order could be settled. The driver who scanned the card might not be the driver for the order that gets settled.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe assumption was one active order per customer at a time, which is reasonable but not enforced at the DB level.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nWrong order settled, wrong driver paid, wrong escrow released. Low probability but high financial impact.\n\n**FIX:**\nEither enforce a DB constraint (one in-transit order per customer at a time) or require the driver to specify the order ID when using card confirmation. The latter is safer.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (low probability)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 12\n\n**TITLE:** Gas shortfall refund uses hardcoded `\"Lagos\"` region for LPG price lookup\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/ledger.go` line ~175\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\nlpgPriceKobo, err := s.liveLPGPriceKobo(ctx, tx, \"Lagos\")\n```\nThe region is hardcoded to `\"Lagos\"`. When SpeedPlus expands to Abuja, Port Harcourt, or other cities, the shortfall refund will always use Lagos pricing regardless of where the delivery occurred.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nLagos-first launch, hardcoded for simplicity.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nWrong shortfall refund amounts for non-Lagos orders. Merchants in other cities could be over- or under-compensated.\n\n**FIX:**\nDerive the region from the order's delivery address or the merchant's location. Pass it through to `liveLPGPriceKobo`.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (Lagos-only launch)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 13\n\n**TITLE:** No API versioning strategy beyond `/api/v1` — breaking changes will be painful\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / API Design\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/cmd/server/main.go` router setup\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nAll routes are under `/api/v1`. There is no `/api/v2` or any mechanism for versioning individual endpoints. When breaking changes are needed (e.g., changing the order response shape), all clients must be updated simultaneously.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nV1 is fine for launch, but there's no documented strategy for what happens when V2 is needed.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nFuture breaking changes will require coordinated deploys of all four frontend apps simultaneously, or maintaining backward compatibility indefinitely.\n\n**FIX:**\nDocument the versioning strategy now. For launch, V1 is fine. But establish the rule: new versions get new prefixes, old versions are deprecated with a sunset date.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 14\n\n**TITLE:** No request body size limit — large payloads can cause memory exhaustion\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security / DevOps\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/cmd/server/main.go` — Gin router setup\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThere is no `http.MaxBytesReader` or Gin body size limit configured. A malicious client can send a multi-GB request body to any endpoint, potentially exhausting server memory.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nNot configured.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nA single large request can OOM the API server.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd to the Gin router setup:\n```go\nr.MaxMultipartMemory = 8 << 20 // 8MB\n```\nAnd wrap the server's handler with `http.MaxBytesReader` or use Gin's built-in body limit middleware.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (but easy to fix)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 15\n\n**TITLE:** Subscription `chargeOne` creates orders without verifying merchant is open or KYC-approved\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/subscription.go` `chargeOne()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe subscription auto-charge creates orders by calling `orderSvc.Create()`, which does check `merchant.IsOpen`. However, if the merchant is closed at 6 AM when the cron runs, the subscription charge will fail with `ErrMerchantClosed`, increment the dunning counter, and potentially pause the subscription after 3 failures. A merchant who closes overnight will cause all their subscribers to get dunning strikes.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe subscription cron runs at 6 AM WAT, which is before most merchants open.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nCustomers get their subscriptions paused because their merchant was closed at 6 AM. This is a bad experience and will generate support tickets.\n\n**FIX:**\nEither run the subscription cron at a time when merchants are open (e.g., 9 AM), or add logic to retry subscription charges during business hours rather than immediately dunning.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 4 — FRONTEND ENGINEERING REVIEW\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 16\n\n**TITLE:** Merchant app bank account form accepts user-supplied account name — no verification UI\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/merchant/app/page.tsx` bank form, `bankDraft` state\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe merchant withdrawal form has a free-text `accountName` input. The merchant types their own account name. There is no \"verify account\" step that calls the backend to resolve the name from the bank. This means the UI actively encourages entering unverified data, even if the backend were to add verification.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe verification API call was not implemented on either frontend or backend.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nMerchants can enter any account name. Combined with Issue 4 (backend not verifying), this is a complete gap in payout security.\n\n**FIX:**\nReplace the `accountName` field with a \"Verify account\" button that calls the backend, which calls the payment provider, and returns the verified name for display. The merchant confirms the name before saving.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes (same as Issue 4)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 17\n\n**TITLE:** Driver app cashout uses wallet balance as EWA amount — may include non-earned funds\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/driver/app/page.tsx` `handleCashout()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```typescript\nawait earningsApi.cashout(walletData.balanceKobo, key);\n```\nThe driver cashout uses the full wallet balance as the cashout amount. But the wallet balance includes all credits (tips, bonuses, referrals), not just earned delivery fees. The backend `EWACashout` checks `SumUnpaidEarnings` against the requested amount, so if the wallet balance exceeds unpaid earnings, the cashout will fail with \"insufficient earned balance.\" The driver sees a confusing error.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe frontend doesn't distinguish between earned balance and total wallet balance.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nDrivers who have received tips or bonuses will get confusing errors when trying to cash out their full balance.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd a separate `GET /earnings/balance` endpoint that returns the cashout-eligible amount, and use that in the UI instead of the wallet balance.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 18\n\n**TITLE:** Customer app home page fetches all orders on mount with no auth guard — unauthenticated users get API errors\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/customer/app/page.tsx` lines ~70–74\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```typescript\nuseEffect(() => {\n    ordersApi.list({}).then((data) => { ... }).catch(() => {});\n}, []);\n```\nThe home page calls `ordersApi.list()` on mount with a silent catch. If the user is not authenticated, this will fail silently. The `auth-guard.tsx` component exists but the home page doesn't use it — it relies on the API call failing silently. This means unauthenticated users see the home page with no active order banner, which is correct, but the API call is wasted and could cause confusion if the error is ever surfaced.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe home page was designed to work for both authenticated and unauthenticated users, but the auth check is implicit.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nMinor — silent failure is handled. But it's a code smell and could cause issues if the error handling changes.\n\n**FIX:**\nCheck auth state before making the API call, or use the auth guard component.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 19\n\n**TITLE:** Merchant portal has no empty state for orders tab on first load — shows \"No orders yet\" immediately\n\n**SEVERITY:** Low\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/merchant/app/page.tsx` orders tab\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nWhen a merchant first logs in and has no orders, the orders tab immediately shows \"No orders yet.\" There's no onboarding guidance, no \"here's what to do next\" prompt, no link to set up their store. New merchants will be confused.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nEmpty states were not designed for the onboarding flow.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nPoor first-time merchant experience. Merchants may think something is broken.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd an onboarding checklist for new merchants: \"Complete your profile → Add products → Go online → Wait for orders.\"\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 20\n\n**TITLE:** No loading skeleton on driver app offer card — offer appears with a jarring pop-in\n\n**SEVERITY:** Low\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/driver/app/page.tsx`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nWhen a new offer arrives via WebSocket, it appears instantly with a `slideDown` animation. But if the driver's phone is on a slow connection, the WebSocket message arrives but the offer card renders with potentially stale data (e.g., pickup address not yet resolved). There's no loading state for the offer card.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe offer data comes fully populated from the WebSocket message, so no loading state was needed. But the UX could be smoother.\n\n**IMPACT:** Minor UX issue.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 5 — UI/UX PRODUCT DESIGN REVIEW\n\n### Customer App\n\n**Strengths:**\n- Clean dark-green brand identity, consistent design language\n- Intent-based search is a smart differentiator\n- Active order resume banner is excellent UX\n- Wallet page is well-designed with DVA account display\n\n**Gaps:**\n- No onboarding flow for new users (no tutorial, no \"how it works\")\n- No address management UI visible from the home screen\n- No \"track order\" deep link from notifications\n- Gas cylinder registration flow exists but is buried\n- No loyalty points display on home screen (only accessible via quick link)\n- Gift cards page exists but there's no way to purchase"

A few claims are very specific (line numbers, exact behavior, \"money is debited then reversed\", etc.) and should be confirmed before changing architecture.\nThe report actually shows SpeedPlus is much further along than many startups at this stage.\nThe architecture choices are relatively mature:\ndouble-entry ledger\nescrow\nstate machines\nidempotency\nPostGIS dispatch\nWebSockets\nKYC\nmultiple payment providers\naudit logs\n\nThe biggest problems are not \"the app doesn't work\". They are operational gaps that will destroy trust when real money and real users enter the system.\n\nMy Principal Engineer Assessment\nCurrent status: CONDITIONAL GO\n\nI would not launch publicly yet.\n\nI would allow:\n\n✅ internal testing\n✅ closed beta\n✅ 50-200 users pilot\n\nI would not allow:\n\n❌ public marketing push\n❌ thousands of customers\n❌ real driver fleet onboarding\n\nuntil the following are fixed.\n\nPriority 0 — Launch Blockers (Fix First)\n1. Driver payouts are broken\n\nSeverity: CRITICAL\n\nThis is the biggest issue.\n\nSpeedPlus is a marketplace.\n\nA marketplace has two sides:\n\ndemand (customers)\nsupply (drivers/merchants)\n\nIf drivers cannot withdraw money:\n\nYour supply side dies.\n\nThe flow:\n\nCustomer pays\n      ↓\nEscrow\n      ↓\nDelivery completed\n      ↓\nDriver earns\n      ↓\nDriver withdraws\n      ↓\nBank account\n\nCurrently:\n\nDriver earns\n      ↓\nWallet balance increases\n      ↓\nWithdrawal requested\n      ↓\nERROR\n\nThis is a launch stopper.\n\nFix order:\n\nBackend\n\nCreate:\n\ndriver_bank_accounts\n\nExample:\n\nid\ndriver_id\nbank_code\naccount_number_encrypted\nresolved_name\nprovider\nverified_at\ncreated_at\n\nAdd:\n\nPOST /driver/bank-account/verify\n\nPOST /driver/bank-account\n\nFlow:\n\nDriver enters:\n\nBank: GTBank\nAccount number: 0123456789\n\nBackend:\n\nPaystack Resolve Account\n        |\n        |\nreturns:\nJohn Doe\n\nDriver confirms.\n\nSave.\n\n2. Bank verification is a financial risk\n\nThis affects merchants and drivers.\n\nCurrently:\n\nUser says:\n\nAccount name:\nJohn Smith\n\n\nSystem:\nOkay 👍\n\nThat is dangerous.\n\nCorrect:\n\nUser enters:\n\nAccount number\nBank\n\n\nSystem:\n\nProvider API\n\nReturns:\n\nJOHN ADEBAYO\n\n\nUser confirms\n\nNever trust user-entered names.\n\n3. OSRM production readiness\n\nThis is underestimated.\n\nThe app depends on:\n\ndistance\npricing\nETA\ndispatch\n\nEverything depends on routing.\n\nCurrently:\n\nDevelopment:\n\nAPI\n |\nPublic OSRM\n |\nInternet\n\nProduction needs:\n\nAPI\n |\nPrivate OSRM\n |\nNigeria map data\n\nBefore launch:\n\nTest:\n\nLagos\nAbuja\nIbadan\nPort Harcourt\n\nCheck:\n\npickup → destination\n\ndistance returned?\nETA realistic?\n4. Customer support\n\nI agree with this finding.\n\nThis is actually more important in Nigeria than many engineers realize.\n\nYour first 1,000 users will have:\n\nwrong addresses\nunavailable vendors\ndriver complaints\npayment confusion\nrefund requests\n\nWithout support:\n\nUsers don't think:\n\n\"SpeedPlus has a support issue.\"\n\nThey think:\n\n\"SpeedPlus is a scam.\"\n\nMinimum viable support:\n\nBefore launch:\n\nOrder screen:\n\nNeed help?\n\n[Report issue]\n\nOptions:\n\n- Driver didn't arrive\n- Wrong item\n- Missing item\n- Payment issue\n- Other\n\nThen:\n\nTemporary solution:\n\nWhatsApp support integration\n\nLater:\n\nticketing system\nSecurity Fixes\n5. PIN protection\n\nI agree completely.\n\nYour financial model makes PIN security critical.\n\nCurrent:\n\n4 digit PIN\n\n10,000 combinations\n\nRate limit:\n20/min\n\nBad.\n\nFix:\n\nDatabase:\n\nwallet_pin_attempts\n\nuser_id\nattempt_count\nlocked_until\n\nRules:\n\n5 failures\n\n↓\n\nlock 30 minutes\n\n↓\n\nOTP unlock\n\nAlso:\n\nHigh-risk actions:\n\nRequire:\n\nPIN\nOTP\ndevice verification\nMedium Priority But Important\n6. Admin analytics\n\nThe report marked this as missing.\n\nI agree.\n\nBut don't build a fancy dashboard yet.\n\nYou need operational metrics:\n\nDay one:\n\nOrders today\n\nGMV\n\nRevenue\n\nActive drivers\n\nActive merchants\n\nFailed payments\n\nRefunds\n\nAverage delivery time\n\nCancellation rate\n\nThat is enough.\n\n7. Driver navigation\n\nNot a blocker.\n\nActually, many logistics companies start this way.\n\nUsing:\n\nGoogle Maps\nApple Maps\nWaze\n\nis acceptable.\n\nBuild internal navigation later.\n\nProduct Manager Review\n\nThe strongest part of SpeedPlus:\n\nThe marketplace architecture.\n\nThe weak point:\n\nThe product experience.\n\nRight now it sounds like an engineering-heavy product.\n\nYou built infrastructure.\n\nNow build trust.\n\nMissing customer trust features\n\nBefore launch add:\n\nOrder timeline\n\nExample:\n\nOrder placed ✓\n\nMerchant confirmed ✓\n\nDriver assigned ✓\n\nDriver delivery\n\nGood you already have codes.\n\nAdd:\n\ndelivery photo\ntimestamp\nGPS\nBusiness Audit\n\nThe model:\n\nFood + groceries + pharmacy + gas + courier\n\nis ambitious.\n\nThe risk:\n\nToo many verticals.\n\nOperationally:\n\nFood:\n\nrequires speed\n\nGas:\n\nrequires compliance\n\nPharmacy:\n\nrequires trust\n\nCourier:\n\nrequires reliability\n\nI would launch:\n\nPhase                     "Text": "=== Operation 1 Result (Text) ===\n}\n\n// SaveBankAccount — POST /merchant/bank-account\n// The frontend must resolve the account name via Paystack's /bank/resolve\n// endpoint before calling this. The resolved name is sent in the request\n// body and stored as-is — it is the provider's authoritative answer.\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) SaveBankAccount(c *gin.Context) {\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tBankCode      string `json:\"bankCode\"      binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tBankName      string `json:\"bankName\"      binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tAccountNumber string `json:\"accountNumber\" binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tAccountName   string `json:\"accountName\"   binding:\"required\"` // provider-resolved\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tacct, err := h.merchant.SaveBankAccount(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c),\n\t\treq.BankCode, req.BankName, req.AccountNumber, req.AccountName)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\n\t\t\"bankCode\":      acct.BankCode,\n\t\t\"bankName\":      acct.BankName,\n\t\t\"accountNumber\": acct.AccountNumber,\n\t\t\"accountName\":   acct.AccountName,\n\t}))\n}\n\n// Withdraw — POST /merchant/withdraw\n// Debits the merchant wallet and enqueues a bank transfer via the asynq worker.\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) Withdraw(c *gin.Context) {\n\tidempotencyKey := c.GetHeader(\"Idempotency-Key\")\n\tif idempotencyKey == \"\" {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"Idempotency-Key header required\", \"Idempotency-Key\"))\n\n=== Operation 2 Result (Text) ===\n\t\treturn nil, nil // no account saved yet — not an error\n\t}\n\treturn acct, nil\n}\n\n// SaveBankAccount upserts the merchant's withdrawal bank account.\n// accountName must be pre-resolved by the caller via the payment provider's\n// account-resolution API — this function trusts it as already verified.\nfunc (s *MerchantService) SaveBankAccount(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID, bankCode, bankName, accountNumber, accountName string) (*model.MerchantBankAccount, error) {\n\tmerchant, err := s.ResolveByUserID(ctx, userID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tacct := &model.MerchantBankAccount{\n\t\tMerchantID:    merchant.ID,\n\t\tBankCode:      bankCode,\n\t\tBankName:      bankName,\n\t\tAccountNumber: accountNumber,\n\t\tAccountName:   accountName,\n\t\tIsVerified:    true,\n\t}\n\tif err := s.merchants.UpsertBankAccount(ctx, acct); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn acct, nil\n}"

                      "stdout": "'use client';\n\nimport { useEffect, useState, useTransition } from 'react';\nimport { adminApi, type OrderSummary, type OrderDetail } from '@speedplus/api-client';\nimport { Badge } from '@speedplus/ui';\n\nfunction formatKobo(k: number) {\n  return `₦${(k / 100).toLocaleString('en-NG', { minimumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;\n}\n\nexport default function OrdersPage() {\n  const [orders, setOrders] = useState<OrderSummary[]>([]);\n  const [detail, setDetail] = useState<OrderDetail | null>(null);\n  const [q, setQ] = useState('');\n  const [status, setStatus] = useState('');\n  const [error, setError] = useState('');\n  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    adminApi.searchOrders(q || undefined, status || undefined)\n      .then((d) => setOrders(d.orders))\n      .catch((e: Error) => setError(e.message));\n  }, [q, status]);\n\n  function openDetail(id: string) {\n    adminApi.getOrderDetail(id)\n      .then(setDetail)\n      .catch((e: Error) => setError(e.message));\n  }\n\n  function handleAssign(orderId: string) {\n    const driverId = window.prompt('Driver UUID:');\n    if (!driverId) return;\n    startTransition(async () => {\n      try {\n        await adminApi.assignDriver(orderId, driverId);\n        setDetail(null);\n      } catch (e: unknown) {\n        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Failed');\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  if (detail) {\n    return (\n      <div className=\"px-8 py-7 flex flex-col gap-4\">\n        <button onClick={() => setDetail(null)} className=\"text-sm text-mid hover:text-emerald transition-colors\">← Back</button>\n        <h1 className=\"font-display font-semibold text-[22px]\">Order {detail.id.slice(0, 8)}…</h1>\n        <div className=\"grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 text-sm\">\n          <span><b>Status:</b> {detail.status}</span>\n          <span><b>Total:</b> {formatKobo(detail.totalKobo)}</span>\n          <span><b>Vertical:</b> {detail.vertical}</span>\n          <span><b>Driver:</b> {detail.driverId ?? 'Unassigned'}</span>\n        </div>\n        {!detail.driverId && (\n          <button\n            disabled={isPending}\n            onClick={() => handleAssign(detail.id)}\n            className=\"self-start font-display text-xs font-semibold text-emerald bg-lime rounded-[10px] px-4 py-2 hover:bg-lime-600 transition-colors disabled:opacity-50\"\n          >\n            Assign Driver\n          </button>\n        )}\n        <h2 className=\"font-display font-semibold text-[16px] mt-2\">Timeline</h2>\n        <ol className=\"flex flex-col gap-2\">\n          {detail.events.map((ev) => (\n            <li key={ev.id} className=\"flex gap-3 text-sm\">\n              <span className=\"text-mid w-36 shrink-0\">{new Date(ev.createdAt).toLocaleTimeString()}</span>\n              <span>\n                <b>{ev.actorRole}</b> · {ev.fromStatus || '—'} → <b>{ev.toStatus}</b>\n                {ev.note && <span className=\"text-mid\"> ({ev.note})</span>}\n              </span>\n            </li>\n          ))}\n        </ol>\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  return (\n---\n'use client';\n\nimport { useState, useTransition } from 'react';\nimport { adminApi, type LedgerEntry } from '@speedplus/api-client';\n\nfunction formatKobo(k: number) {\n  const sign = k >= 0 ? '+' : '';\n  return `${sign}₦${(Math.abs(k) / 100).toLocaleString('en-NG', { minimumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;\n}\n\nexport default function LedgerPage() {\n  const [userId, setUserId] = useState('');\n  const [entries, setEntries] = useState<LedgerEntry[]>([]);\n  const [cursor, setCursor] = useState<string | undefined>();\n  const [hasMore, setHasMore] = useState(false);\n  const [error, setError] = useState('');\n  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n\n  function load(nextCursor?: string) {\n    startTransition(async () => {\n      try {\n        const d = await adminApi.getLedger(userId, nextCursor);\n        if (nextCursor) {\n          setEntries((prev) => [...prev, ...d.entries]);\n        } else {\n          setEntries(d.entries);\n        }\n        setHasMore(d.entries.length === 50);\n        if (d.entries.length > 0) {\n          setCursor(d.entries[d.entries.length - 1]!.id);\n        }\n        setError('');\n      } catch (e: unknown) {\n        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Failed');\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"px-8 py-7 flex flex-col gap-4\">",

          "content": "Good. I now have verified ground truth on every major claim. Here's the honest reconciliation.\n\n---\n\n## Verification Results: What's Real vs. What Needs Nuance\n\n### ✅ Confirmed as stated\n\n**Driver cashout is broken** — `wallet.go:632` literally returns `\"driver bank account resolution not yet implemented\"`. No driver bank account table, no API endpoint, no UI. Confirmed completely absent across backend, API client, and driver app.\n\n**PIN has no brute-force protection** — No `pin_attempts` table in any migration, no lockout logic in `auth.go` or `paycode.go`. The `scan-card` endpoint sits under the `paycodes` group rate limit (20/min, per-IP). Confirmed.\n\n**OSRM is production-ready** — The audit report was wrong here. `apps/osrm/start.sh` and `Dockerfile` exist and are fully implemented: downloads Nigeria OSM data from Geofabrik, runs `osrm-extract`, `osrm-partition`, `osrm-customize`, starts `osrm-routed`. The config guard in `config.go` blocks the public demo in production. **OSRM is not a blocker** — it just needs a Railway/Fly deployment with a persistent volume.\n\n**Bank account name is not server-verified** — The handler comment says \"The frontend must resolve the account name via Paystack's /bank/resolve endpoint before calling this.\" But there is no `/bank/resolve` endpoint in the backend, no `ResolveAccount` method in the Paystack provider, and the merchant frontend has a free-text `accountName` input with no verification step. The backend trusts whatever the frontend sends. Confirmed gap.\n\n**Admin has no analytics dashboard** — `admin/app/page.tsx` is a single-line redirect to `/kyc`. No GMV, no revenue, no order counts. The admin has operational tools (orders, disputes, ledger viewer) but zero aggregate metrics. Confirmed.\n\n**No customer support path** — Confirmed absent across all four frontend apps and the backend.\n\n### ⚠️ Audit report was partially wrong\n\n**OSRM** — The report said \"no evidence of a production OSRM deployment.\" Wrong. The Dockerfile and start script are complete and correct. This is a deployment task, not a build task. Estimated effort: 2 hours to deploy on Railway with a persistent volume.\n\n**Bank account verification** — The report said `IsVerified` defaults to `true` \"without any actual verification step.\" Technically accurate, but the handler comment documents the intended contract (frontend resolves first). The gap is that the backend has no `/bank/resolve` proxy endpoint and the frontend doesn't call one. The fix is smaller than the report implied — you don't need to redesign the flow, you need to add one endpoint and update the UI.\n\n---\n\n## Verified Priority List\n\nHere's what to actually build, in order, with honest scope estimates.\n\n---\n\n### Priority 0 — True Launch Blockers\n\n**1. Driver bank account + cashout**\n\nThis is the only thing that is genuinely broken end-to-end. Everything else is a gap or a risk. This is a hard failure.\n\nWhat's needed:\n- Migration: `driver_bank_accounts` table\n- Backend: `POST /driver/bank-account/verify` (proxies Paystack resolve), `POST /driver/bank-account`, `GET /driver/bank-account`\n- Backend: implement `ResolveCashoutRecipient` for drivers\n- API client: add driver bank account endpoints\n- Driver app: add bank account setup UI in the Earn tab\n\nEstimated effort: 2–3 days.\n\n**2. Bank account name server-side resolution (merchants + drivers)**\n\nThe backend needs to own the resolution call, not delegate it to the frontend. A malicious frontend can send any name.\n\nWhat's needed:\n- Add `ResolveAccount(ctx, bankCode, accountNumber string) (string, error)` to the Paystack provider\n- Add `POST /merchant/bank-account/resolve` endpoint that calls it and returns the name\n- Update `SaveBankAccount` to call resolve internally and ignore the client-supplied name\n- Update merchant UI to call resolve before showing the confirmation step\n\nEstimated effort: 1 day.\n\n**3. PIN brute-force protection**\n\nWhat's needed:\n- Migration: add `attempt_count int`, `locked_until timestamptz` to `pins` table\n- Update `VerifyPIN` to increment on failure, lock after 5, check lock before comparing\n- Add OTP-based unlock endpoint\n- Update `ConfirmByCard` to use the same lockout check\n\nEstimated effort: 1 day.\n\n**4. Customer support path**\n\nMinimum viable: a \"Report issue\" button on the order screen that opens a pre-filled WhatsApp link or mailto. No backend needed for the pilot.\n\nEstimated effort: 2 hours.\n\n---\n\n### Priority 1 — Fix Before Scaling\n\n**5. OSRM production deployment**\n\nThe code is done. This is purely operational.\n\nSteps:\n1. Create a Railway service with a persistent volume at `/data`\n2. Deploy `apps/osrm` with the existing Dockerfile\n3. First boot downloads and processes Nigeria map (~2GB, ~20 min)\n4. Set `OSRM_URL` in production env to the Railway internal URL\n\nEstimated effort: 2 hours.\n\n**6. Admin operational metrics**\n\nDon't build a dashboard. Build a single page with the numbers you need to run the business on day one.\n\nWhat's needed:\n- One backend endpoint: `GET /admin/metrics` returning today's order count, GMV, revenue, active drivers, active merchants, failed payments, cancellation count\n- One admin page that displays them\n\nEstimated effort: 1 day.\n\n**7. Leaked Sendbyte key**\n\nRotate the key immediately. Remove the duplicate line from `.env`. Add `QUOTE_SECRET`, `PAYCODE_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` to `.env`.\n\nEstimated effort: 30 minutes.\n\n---\n\n### Priority 2 — Before Public Marketing Push\n\n**8. Fraud velocity checks**\n\nThe rate limiter fails open on Redis errors (auth endpoints). Fix: pass a `failClosed bool` to `RateLimit`, set it true for `/auth` and `/otp` groups.\n\n**9. Order timeline UI for customers**\n\nThe backend already emits `order_events` and WebSocket status changes. The customer app just needs a timeline component on the order detail screen showing each status transition with a timestamp.\n\n**10. Driver identity on customer tracking screen**\n\nThe backend already returns `driverName`, `driverRating`, `driverVehicle`, `driverPhone` in `ToResponse()`. The customer tracking page just needs to display them.\n\n---\n\n## Corrected Scores\n\n| Area | Original Score | Verified Score | Notes |\n|------|---------------|----------------|-------|\n| Backend architecture | 85 | 85 | Solid. Double-entry ledger, state machines, idempotency all correct |\n| Financial architecture | 80 | 78 | Driver cashout broken drops this |\n| Security | 65 | 62 | PIN lockout absent, bank name unverified, leaked key |\n| Frontend | 75 | 73 | Bank form gap confirmed |\n| UX | 70 | 68 | No support path, no order timeline |\n| Operations | 60 | 65 | OSRM is actually ready to deploy, not missing |\n| Business readiness | 75 | 72 | Driver supply side can't get paid |\n\n**Overall: 76/100**\n\n**Decision: CONDITIONAL GO for closed beta (50–200 users), NO GO for public launch.**\n\nThe foundation is genuinely strong. The ledger is correct, the escrow model is sound, the state machines are properly enforced, idempotency is implemented throughout. None of the blockers require architectural changes — they're all missing features or missing deployments. The critical path to public launch is roughly 5–6 focused engineering days."

            "prompt": "I have reviewed the audit output and the verification results. The important thing is that the second pass corrected some false positives, which is exactly what a principal engineer should do before assigning production blockers.\n\nThe current situation is:\n\n# SpeedPlus Production Decision\n\n## Current Verdict\n\n**Closed Beta Ready ✅**\n**Public Production Launch Not Ready ❌**\n\nThe architecture is actually stronger than many early-stage marketplaces. The biggest risk is not code quality — it is **operational completeness and money movement correctness**.\n\nThe system can probably survive 50–200 controlled users.\n\nIt should not yet handle thousands of customers, merchants, and drivers.\n\n---\n\n# What I would fix before production launch (ordered)\n\n## P0 — Must Fix Before Any Real Users Pay Money\n\n---\n\n# 1. Driver payout system is broken\n\n## Current problem\n\nA driver completes deliveries.\n\nMoney enters the driver wallet.\n\nDriver clicks withdraw.\n\nThe system reaches:\n\n```go\nreturn \"\", \"\", \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"driver bank account resolution not yet implemented\")\n```\n\nMeaning:\n\n* driver earned money ✅\n* wallet balance exists ✅\n* cashout request created ✅\n* actual bank transfer ❌\n\nThe rider cannot receive money.\n\n## Business impact\n\nThis kills supply.\n\nA delivery marketplace is a three-sided business:\n\nCustomer → Merchant → Driver\n\nIf drivers cannot withdraw:\n\n* riders stop accepting jobs\n* WhatsApp complaints start\n* trust collapses\n\n## Fix\n\nBuild:\n\n### Database\n\n```\ndriver_bank_accounts\n\nid\ndriver_id\nbank_code\nbank_name\naccount_number\naccount_name\nverified\ncreated_at\nupdated_at\n```\n\n### Backend\n\nAdd:\n\n```\nPOST /driver/bank-account/resolve\n\nPOST /driver/bank-account\n\nGET /driver/bank-account\n```\n\nFlow:\n\nDriver enters:\n\n```\nBank: GTBank\nAccount Number: 0123456789\n```\n\nBackend calls Paystack:\n\n```\nresolve account\n```\n\nReturns:\n\n```\nAccount Name:\nAJAYI OBA...\n```\n\nDriver confirms.\n\nSave.\n\nThen:\n\n```\nResolveCashoutRecipient()\n```\n\nbecomes:\n\n```\nif driver {\n   get verified bank account\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# 2. Bank verification architecture is wrong\n\nCurrent assumption:\n\nFrontend verifies.\n\nThis is dangerous.\n\nAnything from frontend is untrusted.\n\nA malicious user can send:\n\n```json\n{\n\"accountNumber\":\"1234567890\",\n\"accountName\":\"Dangote\"\n}\n```\n\nBackend accepts it.\n\n## Correct architecture\n\nBackend owns verification.\n\nFlow:\n\n```\nFrontend\n |\n |\nEnter bank details\n |\n |\nBackend\n |\n |\nPaystack Resolve Account API\n |\n |\nVerified name returned\n |\n |\nSave\n```\n\nNever trust:\n\n```\naccountName\n```\n\nfrom frontend.\n\n---\n\n# 3. PIN security\n\nThis one is important because SpeedPlus is becoming a wallet company.\n\nCurrent:\n\n4 digit PIN.\n\nPossible attempts:\n\n```\n0000\n0001\n0002\n...\n9999\n```\n\nNo lock.\n\n## Fix\n\nDatabase:\n\n```\nwallet_pins\n\nfailed_attempts\nlocked_until\n```\n\nLogic:\n\nAttempt 1:\n\n```\nwrong\nfailed_attempts = 1\n```\n\nAttempt 5:\n\n```\nAccount locked\n```\n\nUnlock:\n\nOTP verification.\n\nThis is standard fintech behaviour.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Support system\n\nThe marketplace assumption:\n\n\"Everything works.\"\n\nReality:\n\nSomeone will say:\n\n* driver collected item but disappeared\n* merchant gave wrong food\n* gas quantity is wrong\n* payment deducted but order failed\n\nCurrently:\n\nCustomer has no escape route.\n\n## Minimum launch solution\n\nDo not build Intercom/Zendesk yet.\n\nJust add:\n\nOrder page:\n\n```\nNeed help?\n```\n\nOptions:\n\n```\nWrong item\nDriver issue\nPayment problem\nCancel dispute\nOther\n```\n\nButton:\n\n```\nChat WhatsApp Support\n```\n\nGenerate:\n\n```\nHello SpeedPlus,\nOrder #12345\nIssue:\n```\n\nEnough for MVP.\n\n---\n\n# P1 — Before scaling\n\n---\n\n# 5. OSRM\n\nCorrection:\n\nThe previous audit was wrong.\n\nThe code is already there.\n\nActually good implementation.\n\nYou already have:\n\n* Nigeria OSM download\n* preprocessing\n* MLD algorithm\n* Docker deployment\n\nOnly missing:\n\nInfrastructure.\n\nDeploy:\n\nRailway/Fly.io/AWS ECS.\n\nImportant:\n\nPersistent volume.\n\nBecause processing Nigeria map takes time.\n\nDo not rebuild every deploy.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Admin dashboard\n\nCurrently admin is an operator.\n\nNot a business control center.\n\nYou need:\n\nDaily:\n\n```\nOrders:\n125\n\nGMV:\n₦850,000\n\nRevenue:\n₦75,000\n\nActive drivers:\n34\n\nActive merchants:\n19\n\nFailed payments:\n3\n\nCancellation:\n7%\n```\n\nWithout this, you cannot run the company.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Security hardening\n\nBefore public launch:\n\n## Add:\n\n### Auth rate limiting fail closed\n\nCurrently:\n\nRedis dies.\n\nAuth opens.\n\nBad.\n\nChange:\n\nLogin:\n\nRedis unavailable:\n\n```\n503 temporarily unavailable\n```\n\nNot:\n\n```\nallow everything\n```\n\n---\n\n# Product Manager Review\n\n## Strong points\n\n### 1. Escrow model\n\nVery good.\n\nMost startups get this wrong.\n\nYou have:\n\nCustomer wallet\n\n↓\n\nEscrow\n\n↓\n\nSettlement\n\n↓\n\nMerchant\nDriver\nPlatform\n\nThis is the right marketplace architecture.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Order state machine\n\nStrong.\n\nPreventing:\n\n```\nDelivered → Accepted\n```\n\ntype bugs is important.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Quote signing\n\nExcellent.\n\nStops:\n\nFrontend changing:\n\n```\ndelivery fee = ₦500\n```\n\ninto:\n\n```\ndelivery fee = ₦50\n```\n\n---\n\n# Product gaps\n\n## Customer experience\n\nMissing:\n\n### Order timeline\n\nUsers need:\n\n```\nOrder placed ✓\n\nMerchant accepted ✓\n\nDriver assigned ✓\n\nDriver arriving 🚴\n\nDelivered ✓\n```\n\nCurrently they only know status.\n\n---\n\n## Driver trust\n\nCustomer should see:\n\n```\nJohn\n\n⭐4.8 rating\n\nHonda bike\n\nPlate number ABC123\n```\n\nbefore arrival.\n\n---\n\n## Merchant onboarding\n\nCurrent:\n\nMerchant logs in.\n\nEmpty page.\n\nBetter:\n\nChecklist:\n\n```\n1 Complete profile\n2 Add products\n3 Set opening hours\n4 Go online\n5 Receive first order\n```\n\n---\n\n# Business Audit\n\n## Revenue model\n\nYour structure:\n\nMerchant:\n\n92%\n\nSpeedPlus:\n\n8%\n\nDriver:\n\n80% delivery fee\n\nService fee:\n\n3-5%\n\nThis is reasonable.\n\nBut watch:\n\n## Unit economics\n\nThe biggest danger is delivery subsidy.\n\nExample:\n\nDelivery fee:\n\n₦1500\n\nDriver:\n\n80%\n\n= ₦1200\n\nPlatform:\n\n₦300\n\nBut:\n\nCustomer acquisition:\n\n₦500\n\nSupport:\n\n₦50\n\nPayment fee:\n\n₦30\n\nInfrastructure:\n\n₦20\n\nYou lose money.\n\nYou need contribution margin tracking.\n\n---\n\n# Metrics you need before launch\n\nAdd:\n\n## Customer\n\nCAC\n\nRetention\n\nRepeat orders\n\nAverage order value\n\n## Driver\n\nAcceptance rate\n\nCompletion rate\n\nAverage earnings/hour\n\n## Merchant\n\nOrders/day\n\nCancellation rate\n\nPreparation time\n\n## Business\n\nContribution margin/order\n\nGMV\n\nTake rate\n\nBurn rate\n\n---\n\n# Accounting Audit\n\nYour ledger design is good.\n\nBut add:\n\n## Daily reconciliation job\n\nEvery night:\n\nCompare:\n\n```\nPayment provider transactions\n\nvs\n\nInternal ledger\n\nvs\n\nWallet balances\n```\n\nGenerate:\n\n```\nMatched:\n500 transactions\n\nMismatch:\n3 transactions\n```\n\nFintech companies live and die here.\n\n---\n\n# Final Production Checklist\n\n## Before launch\n\nMust complete:\n\n| Item                   | Priority |\n| ---------------------- | -------- |\n| Driver bank payout     | P0       |\n| Bank verification      | P0       |\n| PIN lockout            | P0       |\n| Support flow           | P0       |\n| OSRM deployment        | P1       |\n| Admin metrics          | P1       |\n| Secrets cleanup        | P1       |\n| Fraud checks           | P2       |\n| Order timeline         | P2       |\n| Driver profile display | P2       |\n\n---\n\n# My principal engineer recommendation\n\nDo **not** spend time rewriting architecture.\n\nThe foundation is good.\n\nDo not migrate frameworks.\n\nDo not split services.\n\nDo not rebuild.\n\nThe next sprint should only be:\n\n## Sprint 1 (5-7 days)\n\n```\nDriver payouts\nBank verification\nPIN security\nSupport\nAdmin metrics\nProduction OSRM\nSecrets rotation\n```\n\nAfter this:\n\nSpeedPlus is technically ready for a controlled public launch.\n\nThe codebase is not (\n\t\"context\"\n\n\t\"github.com/google/uuid\"\n\t\"github.com/speedplus/api/internal/model\"\n\t\"gorm.io/gorm\"\n)\n\ntype MerchantRepo interface {\n\tFindByUserID(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID) (*model.Merchant, error)\n\tFindProfileByUserID(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID) (*model.MerchantProfile, error)\n\tSetOpen(ctx context.Context, merchantID uuid.UUID, isOpen bool) error\n\tFindBankAccount(ctx context.Context, merchantID uuid.UUID) (*model.MerchantBankAccount, error)\n\tUpsertBankAccount(ctx context.Context, acct *model.MerchantBankAccount) error\n}\n\ntype merchantRepo struct{ db *gorm.DB }\n\nfunc NewMerchantRepo(db *gorm.DB) MerchantRepo { return &merchantRepo{db: db} }\n\nfunc (r *merchantRepo) FindByUserID(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID) (*model.Merchant, error) {\n\tvar m model.Merchant\n\terr := r.db.WithContext(ctx).Where(\"user_id = ?\", userID).First(&m).Error\n\treturn &m, err\n}\n\nfunc (r *merchantRepo) FindProfileByUserID(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID) (*model.MerchantProfile, error) {\n\tvar p model.MerchantProfile\n\terr := r.db.WithContext(ctx).Where(\"user_id = ?\", userID).First(&p).Error\n\treturn &p, err\n}\n\nfunc (r *merchantRepo) SetOpen(ctx context.Context, merchantID uuid.UUID, isOpen bool) error {\n\treturn r.db.WithContext(ctx).Model(&model.Merchant{}).\n\t\tWhere(\"id = ?\", merchantID).\n\t\tUpdate(\"is_open\", isOpen).Error\n}\n\nfunc (r *merchantRepo) FindBankAccount(ctx context.Context, merchantID uuid.UUID) (*model.MerchantBankAccount, error) {\n\tvar acct model.MerchantBankAccount\n\terr := r.db.WithContext(ctx).Where(\"merchant_id = ?\", merchantID).First(&acct).Error\n\treturn &acct, err\n}\n\nfunc (r *merchantRepo) UpsertBankAccount(ctx context.Context, acct *model.MerchantBankAccount) error {\n\treturn r.db.WithContext(ctx).\n\t\tWhere(\"merchant_id = ?\", acct.MerchantID).\n\t\tAssign(acct).\n\t\tFirstOrCreate(acct).Error\n}\n\n=== Operation 2 Result (Text) ===\npackage handler\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\n\t\"github.com/gin-gonic/gin\"\n\t\"github.com/google/uuid\"\n\t\"github.com/speedplus/api/internal/middleware\"\n\t\"github.com/speedplus/api/internal/model\"\n\t\"github.com/speedplus/api/internal/service\"\n)\n\n// MerchantHandler is the authenticated merchant's self-service surface:\n// profile/KYC status, open/closed toggle, order queue + fulfillment\n// transitions, and product catalog CRUD. All routes are RequireRole(\"merchant\")\n// and every write is scoped to the caller's own merchant.ID (see\n// MerchantService.ResolveByUserID) — never trusts a merchant ID from the request.\ntype MerchantHandler struct {\n\tmerchant *service.MerchantService\n\torders   *service.OrderService\n\tcatalog  *service.CatalogService\n\twallet   *service.WalletService\n}\n\nfunc NewMerchantHandler(merchant *service.MerchantService, orders *service.OrderService, catalog *service.CatalogService, wallet *service.WalletService) *MerchantHandler {\n\treturn &MerchantHandler{merchant: merchant, orders: orders, catalog: catalog, wallet: wallet}\n}\n\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) userID(c *gin.Context) uuid.UUID {\n\tid, _ := uuid.Parse(c.GetString(middleware.CtxUserID))\n\treturn id\n}\n\n// GetProfile — GET /merchant/profile\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) GetProfile(c *gin.Context) {\n\tmerchant, kyc, err := h.merchant.GetProfile(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tresp := gin.H{\n\t\t\"id\":           merchant.ID,\n\t\t\"businessName\": merchant.BusinessName,\n\t\t\"vertical\":     merchant.Vertical,\n\t\t\"status\":       merchant.Status,\n\t\t\"isOpen\":       merchant.IsOpen,\n\t\t\"rating\":       merchant.Rating,\n\t}\n\tif kyc != nil {\n\t\tresp[\"kycStatus\"] = kyc.Status\n\t} else {\n\t\tresp[\"kycStatus\"] = \"not_started\"\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(resp))\n}\n\n// SetOpen — POST /merchant/status {isOpen: bool}\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) SetOpen(c *gin.Context) {\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tIsOpen bool `json:\"isOpen\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif err := h.merchant.SetOpen(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c), req.IsOpen); err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"isOpen\": req.IsOpen}))\n}\n\n// ListOrders — GET /merchant/orders?status=pending&cursor=...\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) ListOrders(c *gin.Context) {\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar cursor *uuid.UUID\n\tif raw := c.Query(\"cursor\"); raw != \"\" {\n\t\tif id, err := uuid.Parse(raw); err == nil {\n\t\t\tcursor = &id\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\torders, err := h.orders.ListForMerchant(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID, c.Query(\"status\"), cursor, 20)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"orders\": orders}))\n}\n\n// TransitionOrder — POST /merchant/orders/:id/transition {to: \"confirmed\"|\"preparing\"|\"ready_for_pickup\"|\"cancelled\"}\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) TransitionOrder(c *gin.Context) {\n\torderID, err := uuid.Parse(c.Param(\"id\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"Invalid order ID\", \"id\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tTo   string  `json:\"to\" binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tNote *string `json:\"note\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif err := h.orders.Transition(c.Request.Context(), orderID, merchant.ID, \"merchant\", model.OrderStatus(req.To), req.Note); err != nil {\n\t\tif err == service.ErrIllegalTransition {\n\t\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusConflict, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", err.Error(), \"\"))\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, errResp(\"FORBIDDEN\", \"Access denied\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"message\": \"order updated\"}))\n}\n\n// ListProducts — GET /merchant/products (includes unavailable items, unlike the public catalog)\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) ListProducts(c *gin.Context) {\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tproducts, err := h.catalog.ListProductsForMerchant(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"products\": products}))\n}\n\ntype productRequest struct {\n\tName        string  `json:\"name\" binding:\"required\"`\n\tDescription *string `json:\"description\"`\n\tPriceKobo   int64   `json:\"priceKobo\" binding:\"required,min=1\"`\n\tCategory    string  `json:\"category\"`\n\tIsAvailable bool    `json:\"isAvailable\"`\n}\n\n// CreateProduct — POST /merchant/products\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) CreateProduct(c *gin.Context) {\n\tvar req productRequest\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tproduct, err := h.catalog.CreateProduct(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID, service.ProductInput{\n\t\tName: req.Name, Description: req.Description, PriceKobo: req.PriceKobo,\n\t\tCategory: req.Category, IsAvailable: req.IsAvailable,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusCreated, successResp(product))\n}\n\n// UpdateProduct — PUT /merchant/products/:id\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) UpdateProduct(c *gin.Context) {\n\tproductID, err := uuid.Parse(c.Param(\"id\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"Invalid product ID\", \"id\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar req productRequest\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tproduct, err := h.catalog.UpdateProduct(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID, productID, service.ProductInput{\n\t\tName: req.Name, Description: req.Description, PriceKobo: req.PriceKobo,\n\t\tCategory: req.Category, IsAvailable: req.IsAvailable,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, errResp(\"FORBIDDEN\", \"Access denied\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(product))\n}\n\n// SetProductAvailability — POST /merchant/products/:id/availability {available: bool}\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) SetProductAvailability(c *gin.Context) {\n\tproductID, err := uuid.Parse(c.Param(\"id\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"Invalid product ID\", \"id\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tAvailable bool `json:\"available\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif err := h.catalog.SetProductAvailability(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID, productID, req.Available); err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, errResp(\"FORBIDDEN\", \"Access denied\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"available\": req.Available}))\n}\n\n// GetBankAccount — GET /merchant/bank-account\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) GetBankAccount(c *gin.Context) {\n\tacct, err := h.merchant.GetBankAccount(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif acct == nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(nil))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\n\t\t\"bankCode\":      acct.BankCode,\n\t\t\"bankName\":      acct.BankName,\n\t\t\"accountNumber\": acct.AccountNumber,\n\t\t\"accountName\":   acct.AccountName,\n\t\t\"isVerified\":    acct.IsVerified,\n\t}))\n}\n\n// SaveBankAccount — POST /merchant/bank-account\n// The frontend must resolve the account name via Paystack's /bank/resolve\n// endpoint before calling this. The resolved name is sent in the request\n// body and stored as-is — it is the provider's authoritative answer.\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) SaveBankAccount(c *gin.Context) {\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tBankCode      string `json:\"bankCode\"      binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tBankName      string `json:\"bankName\"      binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tAccountNumber string `json:\"accountNumber\" binding:\"required\"`\n\t\tAccountName   string `json:\"accountName\"   binding:\"required\"` // provider-resolved\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tacct, err := h.merchant.SaveBankAccount(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c),\n\t\treq.BankCode, req.BankName, req.AccountNumber, req.AccountName)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\n\t\t\"bankCode\":      acct.BankCode,\n\t\t\"bankName\":      acct.BankName,\n\t\t\"accountNumber\": acct.AccountNumber,\n\t\t\"accountName\":   acct.AccountName,\n\t}))\n}\n\n// Withdraw — POST /merchant/withdraw\n// Debits the merchant wallet and enqueues a bank transfer via the asynq worker.\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) Withdraw(c *gin.Context) {\n\tidempotencyKey := c.GetHeader(\"Idempotency-Key\")\n\tif idempotencyKey == \"\" {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"Idempotency-Key header required\", \"Idempotency-Key\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tAmountKobo     int64  `json:\"amountKobo\"     binding:\"required,min=100000\"` // min ₦1,000\n\t\tPIN            string `json:\"pin\"            binding:\"required,len=4\"`\n\t\tWithdrawalType string `json:\"withdrawalType\"` // \"instant\" | \"standard\" (default)\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif err := h.wallet.MerchantWithdraw(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID, h.userID(c),\n\t\treq.AmountKobo, req.PIN, idempotencyKey, req.WithdrawalType); err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", err.Error(), \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"message\": \"withdrawal initiated\"}))\n}\n\n// ListPrescriptions — GET /merchant/prescriptions?status=pending\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) ListPrescriptions(c *gin.Context) {\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tprescriptions, err := h.catalog.ListPrescriptionsForMerchant(c.Request.Context(), merchant.ID, c.Query(\"status\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"prescriptions\": prescriptions}))\n}\n\n// ReviewPrescription — POST /merchant/prescriptions/:id/review {approve: bool, note?: string}\nfunc (h *MerchantHandler) ReviewPrescription(c *gin.Context) {\n\tprescriptionID, err := uuid.Parse(c.Param(\"id\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"Invalid prescription ID\", \"id\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar req struct {\n\t\tApprove bool    `json:\"approve\"`\n\t\tNote    *string `json:\"note\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {\n\t\tvalidationError(c, err)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tmerchant, err := h.merchant.ResolveByUserID(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, errResp(\"NOT_FOUND\", \"Merchant profile not found\", \"\"))\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tp, err := h.catalog.ReviewPrescription(c.Request.Context(), h.userID(c), merchant.ID, prescriptionID, req.Approve, req.Note)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase errors.Is(err, service.ErrPrescriptionUsed):\n\t\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusConflict, errResp(\"VALIDATION_ERROR\", err.Error(), \"\"))\n\t\tcase errors.Is(err, service.ErrForbidden):\n\t\t\tc.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, errResp(\"FORBIDDEN\", \"Access denied\", \"\"))\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t// Previously every non-conflict error (including DB failures)\n\t\t\t// was collapsed into 403 FORBIDDEN, which is misleading for\n\t\t\t// clients and hid real outages behind an auth-looking error.\n\t\t\tinternalError(c, err)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, successResp(gin.H{\"id\": p.ID, \"status\": p.Status}))\n}"
                  }

                "status": "Success"
              }

                "file_text": "-- Driver bank accounts (mirrors merchant_bank_accounts).\n-- account_name is always resolved via the payment provider — never trusted from the client.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS driver_bank_accounts (\n    id             UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    driver_id      UUID        NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    bank_code      TEXT        NOT NULL,\n    bank_name      TEXT        NOT NULL,\n    account_number TEXT        NOT NULL,\n    account_name   TEXT        NOT NULL, -- provider-resolved, not user-supplied\n    provider       TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'paystack',\n    is_verified    BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT true,\n    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n    updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- PIN lockout: track failed attempts and temporary lock per user.\nALTER TABLE pins\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS failed_attempts INT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS locked_until    TIMESTAMPTZ;\n",
                "summary": "Migration: driver bank accounts table and PIN lockout columns"
              },

                "new_str": "type PIN struct {\n\tID             uuid.UUID  `gorm:\"type:uuid;primaryKey;default:gen_random_uuid()\"`\n\tUserID         uuid.UUID  `gorm:\"type:uuid;uniqueIndex;not null\"`\n\tPINHash        string     `gorm:\"not null\"` // bcrypt\n\tFailedAttempts int        `gorm:\"not null;default:0\"`\n\tLockedUntil    *time.Time // nil = not locked\n\tCreatedAt      time.Time\n\tUpdatedAt      time.Time\n}\n\n// DriverBankAccount stores the verified bank account a driver withdraws to.\n// AccountName is resolved via the payment provider's account-resolution API\n// before saving — never trusted from the request body.\ntype DriverBankAccount struct {\n\tID            uuid.UUID `gorm:\"type:uuid;primaryKey;default:gen_random_uuid()\"`\n\tDriverID      uuid.UUID `gorm:\"type:uuid;uniqueIndex;not null\"`\n\tBankCode      string    `gorm:\"not null\"`\n\tBankName      string    `gorm:\"not null\"`\n\tAccountNumber string    `gorm:\"not null\"`\n\tAccountName   string    `gorm:\"not null\"` // provider-resolved\n\tProvider      string    `gorm:\"not null;default:'paystack'\"`\n\tIsVerified    bool      `gorm:\"not null;default:true\"`\n\tCreatedAt     time.Time\n\tUpdatedAt     time.Time\n}"

              "args": {
                "command": "str_replace",
                "new_str": "// ResolveAccount calls Paystack's /bank/resolve to verify an account number\n// and return the provider-authoritative account name.\nfunc (p *PaystackProvider) ResolveAccount(ctx context.Context, bankCode, accountNumber string) (string, error) {\n\tvar resp struct {\n\t\tStatus bool `json:\"status\"`\n\t\tData   struct {\n\t\t\tAccountName string `json:\"account_name\"`\n\t\t} `json:\"data\"`\n\t\tMessage string `json:\"message\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := p.get(ctx, \"/bank/resolve?account_number=\"+accountNumber+\"&bank_code=\"+bankCode, &resp); err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", err\n\t}\n\tif !resp.Status {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"paystack resolve: %s\", resp.Message)\n\t}\n\treturn resp.Data.AccountName, nil\n}\n\n// ListBanks returns the list of Nigerian banks from Paystack.\nfunc (p *PaystackProvider) ListBanks(ctx context.Context) ([]struct {\n\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\tCode string `json:\"code\"`\n}, error) {\n\tvar resp struct {\n\t\tStatus bool `json:\"status\"`\n\t\tData   []struct {\n\t\t\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\t\t\tCode string `json:\"code\"`\n\t\t} `json:\"data\"`\n\t\tMessage string `json:\"message\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := p.get(ctx, \"/bank?currency=NGN&perPage=100\", &resp); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tif !resp.Status {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"paystack list banks: %s\", resp.Message)\n\t}\n\treturn resp.Data, nil\n}",
                "old_str": "func (p *PaystackProvider) post(ctx context.Context, path string, body interface{}, out interface{}) error {",

              },
              "orig_args": {

                "new_str": "// ResolveAccount calls Paystack's /bank/resolve to verify an account number\n// and return the provider-authoritative account name.\nfunc (p *PaystackProvider) ResolveAccount(ctx context.Context, bankCode, accountNumber string) (string, error) {\n\tvar resp struct {\n\t\tStatus bool `json:\"status\"`\n\t\tData   struct {\n\t\t\tAccountName string `json:\"account_name\"`\n\t\t} `json:\"data\"`\n\t\tMessage string `json:\"message\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := p.get(ctx, \"/bank/resolve?account_number=\"+accountNumber+\"&bank_code=\"+bankCode, &resp); err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", err\n\t}\n\tif !resp.Status {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"paystack resolve: %s\", resp.Message)\n\t}\n\treturn resp.Data.AccountName, nil\n}\n\n// ListBanks returns the list of Nigerian banks from Paystack.\nfunc (p *PaystackProvider) ListBanks(ctx context.Context) ([]struct {\n\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\tCode string `json:\"code\"`\n}, error) {\n\tvar resp struct {\n\t\tStatus bool `json:\"status\"`\n\t\tData   []struct {\n\t\t\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\t\t\tCode string `json:\"code\"`\n\t\t} `json:\"data\"`\n\t\tMessage string `json:\"message\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := p.get(ctx, \"/bank?currency=NGN&perPage=100\", &resp); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tif !resp.Status {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"paystack list banks: %s\", resp.Message)\n\t}\n\treturn resp.Data, nil\n}",

      "assistant": {
        "ToolUse": {
          "message_id": "4e7b845e-142f-45c3-a3a8-264e812d8cac",
          "content": "## 5. AuthService: PIN lockout logic",
          "tool_uses": [
            {
              "id": "tooluse_pKhGNW8nIYff4KPVsk18NK",
              "name": "fs_write",
              "orig_name": "fs_write",
              "args": {
                "command": "str_replace",
                "new_str": "const pinMaxAttempts = 5\nconst pinLockDuration = 30 * time.Minute\n\nfunc (s *AuthService) VerifyPIN(ctx context.Context, userID uuid.UUID, pin string) error {\n\tp, err := s.repo.FindPIN(ctx, userID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"pin not set\")\n\t}\n\tif p.LockedUntil != nil && time.Now().Before(*p.LockedUntil) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"pin locked — too many failed attempts, try again after %s\", p.LockedUntil.Format(\"15:04\"))\n\t}\n\tif bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(p.PINHash), []byte(pin)) != nil {\n\t\tvar lockUntil *time.Time\n\t\tif p.FailedAttempts+1 >= pinMaxAttempts {\n\t\t\tt := time.Now().Add(pinLockDuration)\n\t\t\tlockUntil = &t\n\t\t}\n\t\t_ = s.repo.IncrementPINFailure(ctx, userID, lockUntil)\n\t\tif lockUntil != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"pin locked — too many failed attempts, try again in 30 minutes\")\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"invalid pin\")\n\t}\n\t// Success: reset failure counter.\n\t_ = s.repo.ResetPINFailures(ctx, userID)\n\treturn nil\n}",

                "new_str": "func (s *WalletService) ResolveCashoutRecipient(ctx context.Context, cashout *model.CashoutRequest) (recipientCode, accountName, reason string, err error) {\n\tif cashout.ActorType == \"merchant\" && cashout.MerchantID != nil {\n\t\tbankAcct, err := s.repo.FindMerchantBankAccountTx(ctx, nil, *cashout.MerchantID)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", \"\", \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"merchant bank account: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.provider.Name() == \"monnify\" {\n\t\t\treturn bankAcct.BankCode + \":\" + bankAcct.AccountNumber, bankAcct.AccountName, \"SpeedPlus merchant payout\", nil\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn bankAcct.AccountNumber, bankAcct.AccountName, \"SpeedPlus merchant payout\", nil\n\t}\n\t// Driver payout\n\tbankAcct, err := s.repo.FindDriverBankAccountTx(ctx, nil, cashout.DriverID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", \"\", \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"driver bank account not found — driver must add a bank account before withdrawing: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif s.provider.Name() == \"monnify\" {\n\t\treturn bankAcct.BankCode + \":\" + bankAcct.AccountNumber, bankAcct.AccountName, \"SpeedPlus driver payout\", nil\n\t}\n\treturn bankAcct.AccountNumber, bankAcct.AccountName, \"SpeedPlus driver payout\", nil\n}",

                "new_str": "func (s *WalletService) DB() *gorm.DB               { return nil }\nfunc (s *WalletService) Provider() payment.Provider { return s.provider }\n\n// ── Driver bank account ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n// ResolveDriverBankAccount calls the payment provider to verify an account\n// number and return the authoritative account name. Never trusts the caller.\nfunc (s *WalletService) ResolveDriverBankAccount(ctx context.Context, bankCode, accountNumber string) (string, error) {\n\tps, ok := s.provider.(*payment.PaystackProvider)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"bank account resolution requires Paystack provider\")\n\t}\n\tname, err := ps.ResolveAccount(ctx, bankCode, accountNumber)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"resolve account: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn name, nil\n}\n\n// SaveDriverBankAccount persists a verified bank account for a driver.\n// accountName must come from ResolveDriverBankAccount, never from the client.\nfunc (s *WalletService) SaveDriverBankAccount(ctx context.Context, driverID uuid.UUID, bankCode, bankName, accountNumber, accountName string) (*model.DriverBankAccount, error) {\n\tacct := &model.DriverBankAccount{\n\t\tDriverID:      driverID,\n\t\tBankCode:      bankCode,\n\t\tBankName:      bankName,\n\t\tAccountNumber: accountNumber,\n\t\tAccountName:   accountName,\n\t\tIsVerified:    true,\n\t}\n\tif err := s.users.UpsertDriverBankAccount(ctx, acct); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn acct, nil\n}\n\n// GetDriverBankAccount returns the driver's saved bank account, or nil.\nfunc (s *WalletService) GetDriverBankAccount(ctx context.Context, driverID uuid.UUID) (*model.DriverBankAccount, error) {\n\tacct, err := s.repo.FindDriverBankAccountTx(ctx, nil, driverID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil // not found is not an error on the read path\n\t}\n\treturn acct, nil\n}",

Never trusts the caller.\nfunc (s *WalletService) ResolveDriverBankAccount(ctx context.Context, bankCode, accountNumber string) (string, error) {\n\tps, ok := s.provider.(*payment.PaystackProvider)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"bank account resolution requires Paystack provider\")\n\t}\n\tname, err := ps.ResolveAccount(ctx, bankCode, accountNumber)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"resolve account: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn name, nil\n}\n\n// SaveDriverBankAccount persists a verified bank account for a driver.\n// accountName must come from ResolveDriverBankAccount, never from the client.\nfunc (s *WalletService) SaveDriverBankAccount(ctx context.Context, driverID uuid.UUID, bankCode, bankName, accountNumber, accountName string) (*model.DriverBankAccount, error) {\n\tacct := &model.DriverBankAccount{\n\t\tDriverID:      driverID,\n\t\tBankCode:      bankCode,\n\t\tBankName:      bankName,\n\t\tAccountNumber: accountNumber,\n\t\tAccountName:   accountName,\n\t\tIsVerified:    true,\n\t}\n\tif err := s.users.UpsertDriverBankAccount(ctx, acct); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn acct, nil\n}\n\n// GetDriverBankAccount returns the driver's saved bank account, or nil.\nfunc (s *WalletService) GetDriverBankAccount(ctx context.Context, driverID uuid.UUID) (*model.DriverBankAccount, error) {\n\tacct, err := s.repo.FindDriverBankAccountTx(ctx, nil, driverID)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil // not found is not an error on the read path\n\t}\n\treturn acct, nil\n}",
