    "Now I have a thorough understanding of the entire codebase. Let me compile the full production readiness audit.\n\n---\n\n# SpeedPlus — Production Readiness Audit\n\n**Auditor:** Principal Software Engineer\n**Date:** 2026-07-31\n**Branch:** dev\n**Verdict at a glance:** CONDITIONAL GO — significant issues must be resolved before launch\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 1 — ARCHITECTURE MAP\n\n### System Overview\n\nSpeedPlus is a Nigerian last-mile delivery marketplace with five verticals: food, grocery, pharmacy, gas (LPG), and package courier.\n\n**Monorepo structure (Turborepo + pnpm):**\n- `apps/api` — Go 1.26 backend (Gin, GORM, PostgreSQL, Redis, Asynq)\n- `apps/customer` — Next.js 15 PWA (customer-facing)\n- `apps/driver` — Next.js 15 PWA (rider app)\n- `apps/merchant` — Next.js 15 PWA (merchant portal)\n- `apps/admin` — Next.js 15 admin panel\n- `apps/osrm` — Self-hosted OSRM routing engine (Docker)\n\n**Backend stack:**\n- Language: Go 1.26\n- Framework: Gin\n- ORM: GORM + raw SQL for PostGIS queries\n- DB: PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS + pg_trgm\n- Cache/Queue: Redis 7 + Asynq (background jobs + cron)\n- Auth: JWT (HS256, 15-min access / 30-day refresh with token families)\n- Passwords: Argon2id\n- PINs: bcrypt\n- Payments: Paystack, Flutterwave, Monnify, Bridge.xyz (crypto, feature-flagged)\n- KYC: Prembly\n- Storage: Cloudflare R2\n- Email: Sendbyte\n- Observability: Sentry + structured slog\n- Routing: OSRM (self-hosted in prod, public demo in dev)\n\n**Financial model:**\n- Double-entry ledger (journal entries, escrow holds, wallet balances)\n- Escrow: customer wallet → escrow account → settle to merchant + driver + platform\n- Platform takes: 8% commission on subtotal + service fee (3–5% of subtotal) + delivery margin\n- Driver takes: 80% of delivery fee\n- Merchant takes: 92% of subtotal\n\n**Data flow (order lifecycle):**\n1. Customer gets quote (OSRM distance → fee calculation → HMAC-signed quote)\n2. Customer creates order → escrow hold debits wallet atomically\n3. Dispatch: KNN driver search via PostGIS → offer cascade via WebSocket\n4. Driver accepts → order transitions through state machine\n5. Delivery confirmed via 6-digit code or QR paycode or SpeedPlus card + PIN\n6. Settlement: escrow releases → merchant + driver + platform credited in one balanced journal\n\n**34 migrations** covering identity, catalog, orders, dispatch, wallet/ledger, escrow, paycodes, growth, gas domain, pharmacy, and more.\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 2 — USER JOURNEY AUDIT\n\n### Customer Flow\n\n| Step | Works? | Issues |\n|------|--------|--------|\n| Landing/home | ✅ | Clean, intent-based search |\n| Registration | ✅ | Argon2id, referral, async DVA onboarding |\n| Login | ✅ | Constant-time comparison, timing-safe |\n| OTP verification | ✅ | bcrypt-hashed OTP, 5-min TTL, rate-limited |\n| Profile/address | ✅ | Standard CRUD |\n| Service discovery | ✅ | Public catalog endpoints, full-text search |\n| Cart/order creation | ✅ | Quote validation, idempotency, escrow hold |\n| Payment | ✅ | Paystack/Monnify/Flutterwave/USSD/crypto |\n| Order tracking | ✅ | WebSocket real-time updates |\n| Cancellation | ✅ | Configurable refund rules per status |\n| Refund | ✅ | Full/partial refund engine with merchant/rider comp |\n| History | ✅ | Cursor-paginated |\n| Reviews | ✅ | Post-delivery only, idempotent |\n| Support | ❌ | **No support/chat/ticket system exists** |\n\n**Critical gap:** There is no customer support flow. No in-app chat, no ticket system, no dispute escalation path for customers. When something goes wrong (wrong item, damaged goods, driver no-show), the customer has no recourse within the app.\n\n### Rider Flow\n\n| Step | Works? | Issues |\n|------|--------|--------|\n| Registration | ✅ | Vehicle type/plate required |\n| KYC/verification | ✅ | Prembly integration, admin approval queue |\n| Availability toggle | ✅ | Online/offline with location updates |\n| Receiving jobs | ✅ | WebSocket offer push, 15s TTL cascade |\n| Accepting/rejecting | ✅ | Atomic DB claim prevents double-accept |\n| Navigation | ⚠️ | No in-app navigation/maps — driver must use external app |\n| Pickup/delivery | ✅ | Stage progression, proof capture |\n| Delivery confirmation | ✅ | 6-digit code + QR paycode + card fallback |\n| Earnings | ✅ | Real-time wallet balance |\n| Withdrawal | ⚠️ | Driver bank account resolution not implemented (see issue below) |\n\n**Can two riders accept one order?** No — `AcceptOfferTx` uses `SELECT FOR UPDATE` + conditional UPDATE, only one succeeds.\n\n**Can riders fake completion?** Partially mitigated — delivery code required, GPS flagging exists, but flagging is advisory only (never blocks settlement).\n\n### Merchant Flow\n\n| Step | Works? | Issues |\n|------|--------|--------|\n| Registration | ✅ | |\n| Verification | ✅ | KYC queue |\n| Store setup | ✅ | Products, availability |\n| Order receiving | ✅ | 15s polling + WS |\n| Accept/reject | ✅ | State machine transitions |\n| Settlement | ✅ | Automatic on delivery |\n| Withdrawal | ⚠️ | Account name is user-supplied, not provider-verified (see issue) |\n\n### Admin Flow\n\n| Step | Works? | Issues |\n|------|--------|--------|\n| Dashboard | ✅ | |\n| User/driver/merchant management | ✅ | |\n| KYC approval | ✅ | |\n| Escrow freeze/release | ✅ | Dual-admin approval required |\n| Fee config | ✅ | Append-only, versioned |\n| Audit log | ✅ | All admin actions logged |\n| Reports/analytics | ❌ | **No analytics dashboard, no revenue reports, no export** |\n| Fraud prevention | ⚠️ | Basic rate limiting; no fraud scoring, no velocity checks |\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 3 — BACKEND PRINCIPAL ENGINEERING REVIEW\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 1\n\n**TITLE:** Real Sendbyte API key committed to `.env` file\n\n**SEVERITY:** Critical\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/.env`, line 57\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `.env` file contains a real Sendbyte API key: `sk_test_c6bda5998b8445d88b51892eddd3c5bd1ba74d33`. This is a duplicate entry — the file has `SENDBYTE_API_KEY` defined twice, the second time with what appears to be a real key. Even though `.env` is gitignored, this key exists on disk and may have been committed at some point. The `.env.example` also has a placeholder for this key, but the actual `.env` has a real value.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nDeveloper copy-pasted a real key into the `.env` file and left it there. The duplicate entry suggests it was added carelessly at the bottom.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nIf this key is real and was ever committed to git history, anyone with repo access can send emails as SpeedPlus. Even if not committed, it's a bad practice that normalizes real keys in config files.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Immediately rotate the Sendbyte API key\n2. Remove the duplicate entry from `.env`\n3. Audit git history: `git log --all -p -- apps/api/.env`\n4. Add a pre-commit hook or gitleaks rule to block `sk_test_` or `sk_live_` patterns\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 2\n\n**TITLE:** `.env` file missing `QUOTE_SECRET`, `PAYCODE_SECRET`, and `ENCRYPTION_KEY` — server will panic on boot\n\n**SEVERITY:** Critical\n\n**CATEGORY:** DevOps / Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/.env` (entire file), `apps/api/internal/config/config.go` lines 68–85\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `.env` file (the one developers actually use) is missing `QUOTE_SECRET`, `PAYCODE_SECRET`, and `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. The `config.Load()` function calls `panic()` via `mustEnv()` for `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, and `JWT_SECRET`, and returns errors for the three missing keys. The server will fail to start in any environment where this `.env` is used as-is. The `.env.example` has these keys documented, but the actual `.env` does not.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe `.env` file appears to be an older version that predates the addition of these required secrets. The `.env.example` was updated but the actual `.env` was not synced.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nAny developer or deployment that uses this `.env` directly will get a boot failure. More critically, if someone copies `.env` to production without adding these keys, all package orders with recipient PII will fail, all QR paycodes will fail, and all quote signing will fail.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd the three missing keys to `.env`:\n```\nENCRYPTION_KEY=<generate: openssl rand -hex 16>\nPAYCODE_SECRET=<generate: openssl rand -hex 32>\nQUOTE_SECRET=<generate: openssl rand -hex 32>\n```\nAlso add `MONNIFY_WALLET_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` which is required in production.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 3\n\n**TITLE:** Driver bank account resolution not implemented — driver cashouts will always fail\n\n**SEVERITY:** Critical\n\n**CATEGORY:** Business / Backend\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/wallet.go`, `ResolveCashoutRecipient()`, last line\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\nreturn \"\", \"\", \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"driver bank account resolution not yet implemented\")\n```\nThe `ResolveCashoutRecipient` function explicitly returns an error for drivers. This means every driver EWA cashout and every weekly auto-payout will fail at the worker stage. The money is debited from the driver's wallet, the cashout record is created, but the actual bank transfer will always fail and trigger a reversal. Drivers will never receive money to their bank accounts.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe driver bank account model and resolution logic was not implemented. The merchant path was built but the driver path was left as a stub.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nDrivers cannot get paid. This is a complete business failure for the rider supply side. Drivers will churn immediately when they discover they can't cash out.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Add a `driver_bank_accounts` table (similar to `merchant_bank_accounts`)\n2. Add API endpoints for drivers to save/update their bank account\n3. Implement the driver resolution path in `ResolveCashoutRecipient`\n4. Add a driver bank account UI in the driver app\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 4\n\n**TITLE:** Merchant bank account name is user-supplied, not provider-verified\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security / Finance\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/handler/merchant.go` (SaveBankAccount), `apps/merchant/app/page.tsx` bank form\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `MerchantBankAccount` model has a comment: \"account_name is provider-resolved, not user-supplied.\" However, the merchant portal UI has a free-text `accountName` input field that the merchant fills in manually. There is no evidence in the codebase that the account name is actually verified against the payment provider's account resolution API before saving. The model's `IsVerified` field defaults to `true` without any actual verification step.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe model was designed with the intent to verify, but the verification step was not implemented in the handler or service layer.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nMerchants can enter any account name. Payouts could go to wrong accounts. In Nigeria, bank account name verification (via Paystack's `resolve_account` or Monnify's equivalent) is a standard fraud prevention step. Skipping it exposes the platform to misdirected payouts and social engineering.\n\n**FIX:**\nBefore saving a bank account, call the payment provider's account resolution API:\n- Paystack: `GET /bank/resolve?account_number=...&bank_code=...`\n- Monnify: `GET /api/v1/disbursements/account/validate`\n\nOnly save the provider-returned account name, never the user-supplied one. Return the resolved name to the UI for confirmation before saving.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 5\n\n**TITLE:** No customer support system — users have no recourse when orders fail\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Business / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** Entire codebase — feature absent\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThere is no in-app support flow for customers. No chat, no ticket system, no \"report a problem\" button, no dispute initiation from the customer side. The admin panel has dispute/escrow management, but customers have no way to trigger it. When a delivery goes wrong (wrong item, damaged goods, driver no-show, overcharge), the customer is stuck.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nSupport infrastructure was not built as part of the initial scope.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nIn the Nigerian market, trust is built through responsive support. Without it, the first bad experience will result in a negative social media post. Chargeback rates will be high because customers will dispute with their banks instead of the platform.\n\n**FIX:**\nAt minimum before launch:\n1. Add a \"Report a problem\" button on the order detail screen that opens a WhatsApp chat or email\n2. Add a support contact to the order receipt\n3. Document the dispute escalation process for the admin team\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes (business risk)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 6\n\n**TITLE:** OSRM defaults to public demo server in production — pricing and dispatch will fail under load\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** DevOps / Backend\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/config/config.go` line 57, `apps/api/.env`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe `.env` file has `OSRM_URL=http://router.project-osrm.org`. The config correctly blocks this in production (`config.go` returns an error if `OSRM_URL` is the public demo in production). However, the `docker-compose.yml` OSRM container is a placeholder that just sleeps — it doesn't actually run OSRM. There is no evidence of a production OSRM deployment with Nigerian road data loaded.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nOSRM requires a large preprocessing step (downloading OSM data for Nigeria, running `osrm-extract`, `osrm-partition`, `osrm-customize`) that hasn't been completed.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nWithout a private OSRM instance with Nigerian road data, the server will refuse to start in production (config validation). Even if the public demo is used (by changing the config check), it has no Nigerian road data and will return incorrect distances, causing wrong pricing for every order.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Download Nigeria OSM data from Geofabrik\n2. Run OSRM preprocessing pipeline\n3. Deploy OSRM on Railway/Fly.io with a persistent volume\n4. Set `OSRM_URL` to the private instance in production\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 7\n\n**TITLE:** Rate limiter fails open on Redis errors — auth endpoints unprotected during Redis outage\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/middleware/ratelimit.go` lines 22–25\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\nif err != nil {\n    // fail open — don't block on Redis errors\n    c.Next()\n    return\n}\n```\nWhen Redis is unavailable, the rate limiter allows all requests through. This means during a Redis outage (or a targeted Redis DoS), the auth endpoints (`/auth/login`, `/otp/request`) become completely unprotected. An attacker who can disrupt Redis can then brute-force credentials or OTPs at unlimited rate.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nAvailability was prioritized over security for the rate limiter. This is a reasonable tradeoff for most endpoints but not for auth.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nDuring any Redis disruption, credential stuffing and OTP brute-force attacks become trivially possible.\n\n**FIX:**\nFor auth and OTP endpoints specifically, fail closed (return 503) rather than fail open when Redis is unavailable. For other endpoints, fail open is acceptable. Differentiate by passing a `failClosed bool` parameter to `RateLimit`.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 8\n\n**TITLE:** No PIN brute-force protection — wallet PIN can be guessed indefinitely\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/auth.go` `VerifyPIN()`, `apps/api/internal/service/paycode.go` `ConfirmByCard()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe PIN verification functions (`VerifyPIN`, `ConfirmByCard`) have no attempt counting, no lockout, and no rate limiting beyond the general wallet transfer rate limit (10/min). A 4-digit PIN has 10,000 combinations. At 10 attempts/minute, it can be brute-forced in ~17 hours. The `ConfirmByCard` path has no rate limiting at all — it's on the `/paycodes/scan-card` endpoint which has the general `paycodes` rate limit of 20/min, meaning a 4-digit PIN can be brute-forced in ~8 hours.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nPIN lockout was not implemented.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nAny attacker who obtains a customer's SpeedPlus card QR payload (e.g., by photographing it) can brute-force the PIN and drain the wallet.\n\n**FIX:**\n1. Add a `pin_attempts` counter to the `pins` table\n2. Lock the PIN after 5 failed attempts, requiring OTP to unlock\n3. Add per-user rate limiting on PIN verification (not just per-IP)\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 9\n\n**TITLE:** Idempotency middleware uses `SetNX` without atomic read-then-set — race condition on concurrent identical requests\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Concurrency\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/middleware/idempotency.go` lines 55–70\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe idempotency middleware uses `SetNX` to claim a key. If `SetNX` returns `false` (key exists), it reads the cached response with a separate `GET`. Between the `SetNX` and the `GET`, the key could expire (if the first request failed and set a 2-minute error TTL that just expired) and a second concurrent request could claim it. This is a TOCTOU race. More practically: if the first request is still processing (sentinel value), the second request returns 409 \"in progress\" — which is correct — but if the first request fails and the key expires before the second request's `GET`, the second request will also get `SetNX=false` but then `GET` will return a nil/error, and the code falls through to return 409 \"in progress\" even though nothing is processing.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nRedis doesn't have a native atomic \"get-or-set-with-processing-sentinel\" operation without Lua scripting.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nUnder concurrent load with the same idempotency key, a small window exists where a second request could be incorrectly rejected as \"in progress\" when the first has already completed. For money-moving operations, this could cause a user to think their payment failed when it succeeded.\n\n**FIX:**\nUse a Lua script for atomic check-and-set, or use Redis `GETSET` / `SET NX GET` (Redis 7+) to atomically get the old value while setting the new one.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (low probability, but worth fixing)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 10\n\n**TITLE:** `WeeklyAutoPayout` ignores errors from `ListDriversWithUnpaidEarnings`\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Finance\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/wallet.go` line ~220\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\ndrivers, _ := s.repo.ListDriversWithUnpaidEarnings(ctx)\n```\nThe error is silently discarded. If the DB query fails, `drivers` is nil/empty and the entire weekly payout run silently processes zero drivers. No error is logged, no alert is fired.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nError handling was omitted.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nA DB error during the weekly payout cron will silently skip all driver payouts for that week. Drivers won't be paid. The error won't be visible until drivers complain.\n\n**FIX:**\n```go\ndrivers, err := s.repo.ListDriversWithUnpaidEarnings(ctx)\nif err != nil {\n    return fmt.Errorf(\"weekly payout: list drivers: %w\", err)\n}\n```\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (but high business impact)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 11\n\n**TITLE:** `ConfirmByCard` finds \"active in-transit order\" by customer — wrong order could be settled if customer has multiple concurrent orders\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/paycode.go` `ConfirmByCard()`, `apps/api/internal/repo/paycode.go` `FindActiveInTransitOrder()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe card-based delivery confirmation finds the customer's active in-transit order by `customer_id` alone. If a customer somehow has two in-transit orders (e.g., a subscription order and a manual order both dispatched simultaneously), the wrong order could be settled. The driver who scanned the card might not be the driver for the order that gets settled.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe assumption was one active order per customer at a time, which is reasonable but not enforced at the DB level.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nWrong order settled, wrong driver paid, wrong escrow released. Low probability but high financial impact.\n\n**FIX:**\nEither enforce a DB constraint (one in-transit order per customer at a time) or require the driver to specify the order ID when using card confirmation. The latter is safer.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (low probability)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 12\n\n**TITLE:** Gas shortfall refund uses hardcoded `\"Lagos\"` region for LPG price lookup\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/ledger.go` line ~175\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```go\nlpgPriceKobo, err := s.liveLPGPriceKobo(ctx, tx, \"Lagos\")\n```\nThe region is hardcoded to `\"Lagos\"`. When SpeedPlus expands to Abuja, Port Harcourt, or other cities, the shortfall refund will always use Lagos pricing regardless of where the delivery occurred.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nLagos-first launch, hardcoded for simplicity.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nWrong shortfall refund amounts for non-Lagos orders. Merchants in other cities could be over- or under-compensated.\n\n**FIX:**\nDerive the region from the order's delivery address or the merchant's location. Pass it through to `liveLPGPriceKobo`.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (Lagos-only launch)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 13\n\n**TITLE:** No API versioning strategy beyond `/api/v1` — breaking changes will be painful\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / API Design\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/cmd/server/main.go` router setup\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nAll routes are under `/api/v1`. There is no `/api/v2` or any mechanism for versioning individual endpoints. When breaking changes are needed (e.g., changing the order response shape), all clients must be updated simultaneously.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nV1 is fine for launch, but there's no documented strategy for what happens when V2 is needed.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nFuture breaking changes will require coordinated deploys of all four frontend apps simultaneously, or maintaining backward compatibility indefinitely.\n\n**FIX:**\nDocument the versioning strategy now. For launch, V1 is fine. But establish the rule: new versions get new prefixes, old versions are deprecated with a sunset date.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 14\n\n**TITLE:** No request body size limit — large payloads can cause memory exhaustion\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Security / DevOps\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/cmd/server/main.go` — Gin router setup\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThere is no `http.MaxBytesReader` or Gin body size limit configured. A malicious client can send a multi-GB request body to any endpoint, potentially exhausting server memory.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nNot configured.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nA single large request can OOM the API server.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd to the Gin router setup:\n```go\nr.MaxMultipartMemory = 8 << 20 // 8MB\n```\nAnd wrap the server's handler with `http.MaxBytesReader` or use Gin's built-in body limit middleware.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No (but easy to fix)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 15\n\n**TITLE:** Subscription `chargeOne` creates orders without verifying merchant is open or KYC-approved\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Backend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/api/internal/service/subscription.go` `chargeOne()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe subscription auto-charge creates orders by calling `orderSvc.Create()`, which does check `merchant.IsOpen`. However, if the merchant is closed at 6 AM when the cron runs, the subscription charge will fail with `ErrMerchantClosed`, increment the dunning counter, and potentially pause the subscription after 3 failures. A merchant who closes overnight will cause all their subscribers to get dunning strikes.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe subscription cron runs at 6 AM WAT, which is before most merchants open.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nCustomers get their subscriptions paused because their merchant was closed at 6 AM. This is a bad experience and will generate support tickets.\n\n**FIX:**\nEither run the subscription cron at a time when merchants are open (e.g., 9 AM), or add logic to retry subscription charges during business hours rather than immediately dunning.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 4 — FRONTEND ENGINEERING REVIEW\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 16\n\n**TITLE:** Merchant app bank account form accepts user-supplied account name — no verification UI\n\n**SEVERITY:** High\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / Security\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/merchant/app/page.tsx` bank form, `bankDraft` state\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nThe merchant withdrawal form has a free-text `accountName` input. The merchant types their own account name. There is no \"verify account\" step that calls the backend to resolve the name from the bank. This means the UI actively encourages entering unverified data, even if the backend were to add verification.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe verification API call was not implemented on either frontend or backend.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nMerchants can enter any account name. Combined with Issue 4 (backend not verifying), this is a complete gap in payout security.\n\n**FIX:**\nReplace the `accountName` field with a \"Verify account\" button that calls the backend, which calls the payment provider, and returns the verified name for display. The merchant confirms the name before saving.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** Yes (same as Issue 4)\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 17\n\n**TITLE:** Driver app cashout uses wallet balance as EWA amount — may include non-earned funds\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / Business Logic\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/driver/app/page.tsx` `handleCashout()`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```typescript\nawait earningsApi.cashout(walletData.balanceKobo, key);\n```\nThe driver cashout uses the full wallet balance as the cashout amount. But the wallet balance includes all credits (tips, bonuses, referrals), not just earned delivery fees. The backend `EWACashout` checks `SumUnpaidEarnings` against the requested amount, so if the wallet balance exceeds unpaid earnings, the cashout will fail with \"insufficient earned balance.\" The driver sees a confusing error.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe frontend doesn't distinguish between earned balance and total wallet balance.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nDrivers who have received tips or bonuses will get confusing errors when trying to cash out their full balance.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd a separate `GET /earnings/balance` endpoint that returns the cashout-eligible amount, and use that in the UI instead of the wallet balance.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 18\n\n**TITLE:** Customer app home page fetches all orders on mount with no auth guard — unauthenticated users get API errors\n\n**SEVERITY:** Medium\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/customer/app/page.tsx` lines ~70–74\n\n**PROBLEM:**\n```typescript\nuseEffect(() => {\n    ordersApi.list({}).then((data) => { ... }).catch(() => {});\n}, []);\n```\nThe home page calls `ordersApi.list()` on mount with a silent catch. If the user is not authenticated, this will fail silently. The `auth-guard.tsx` component exists but the home page doesn't use it — it relies on the API call failing silently. This means unauthenticated users see the home page with no active order banner, which is correct, but the API call is wasted and could cause confusion if the error is ever surfaced.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe home page was designed to work for both authenticated and unauthenticated users, but the auth check is implicit.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nMinor — silent failure is handled. But it's a code smell and could cause issues if the error handling changes.\n\n**FIX:**\nCheck auth state before making the API call, or use the auth guard component.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 19\n\n**TITLE:** Merchant portal has no empty state for orders tab on first load — shows \"No orders yet\" immediately\n\n**SEVERITY:** Low\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/merchant/app/page.tsx` orders tab\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nWhen a merchant first logs in and has no orders, the orders tab immediately shows \"No orders yet.\" There's no onboarding guidance, no \"here's what to do next\" prompt, no link to set up their store. New merchants will be confused.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nEmpty states were not designed for the onboarding flow.\n\n**IMPACT:**\nPoor first-time merchant experience. Merchants may think something is broken.\n\n**FIX:**\nAdd an onboarding checklist for new merchants: \"Complete your profile → Add products → Go online → Wait for orders.\"\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n### ISSUE 20\n\n**TITLE:** No loading skeleton on driver app offer card — offer appears with a jarring pop-in\n\n**SEVERITY:** Low\n\n**CATEGORY:** Frontend / UX\n\n**LOCATION:** `apps/driver/app/page.tsx`\n\n**PROBLEM:**\nWhen a new offer arrives via WebSocket, it appears instantly with a `slideDown` animation. There's no loading state for the offer card.\n\n**WHY IT HAPPENED:**\nThe offer data comes fully populated from the WebSocket message, so no loading state was needed. But the UX could be smoother.\n\n**IMPACT:** Minor UX issue.\n\n**PRODUCTION BLOCKER:** No\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 5 — UI/UX PRODUCT DESIGN REVIEW\n\n### Customer App\n\n**Strengths:**\n- Clean dark-green brand identity, consistent design language\n- Intent-based search is a smart differentiator\n- Active order resume banner is excellent UX\n- Wallet page is well-designed with DVA account display\n\n**Gaps:**\n- No onboarding flow for new users (no tutorial, no \"how it works\")\n- No address management UI visible from the home screen\n- No \"track order\" deep link from notifications\n- Gas cylinder registration flow exists but is buried\n- No loyalty points display on home screen (only accessible via quick link)\n- Gift cards page exists but there's no way to purchase\n[Tool uses: none]",

Confirmed.\n\n**OSRM is production-ready** — The audit report was wrong here. `apps/osrm/start.sh` and `Dockerfile` exist and are fully implemented: downloads Nigeria OSM data from Geofabrik, runs `osrm-extract`, `osrm-partition`, `osrm-customize`, starts `osrm-routed`. The config guard in `config.go` blocks the public demo in production. **OSRM is not a blocker** — it just needs a Railway/Fly deployment with a persistent volume.\n\n**Bank account name is not server-verified** — The handler comment says \"The frontend must resolve the account name via Paystack's /bank/resolve endpoint before calling this.\" But there is no `/bank/resolve` endpoint in the backend, no `ResolveAccount` method in the Paystack provider, and the merchant frontend has a free-text `accountName` input with no verification step. The backend trusts whatever the frontend sends. Confirmed gap.\n\n**Admin has no analytics dashboard** — `admin/app/page.tsx` is a single-line redirect to `/kyc`. No GMV, no revenue, no order counts. The admin has operational tools (orders, disputes, ledger viewer) but zero aggregate metrics. Confirmed.\n\n**No customer support path** — Confirmed absent across all four frontend apps and the backend.\n\n### ⚠️ Audit report was partially wrong\n\n**OSRM** — The report said \"no evidence of a production OSRM deployment.\" Wrong. The Dockerfile and start script are complete and correct. This is a deployment task, not a build task. Estimated effort: 2 hours to deploy on Railway with a persistent volume.\n\n**Bank account verification** — The report said `IsVerified` defaults to `true` \"without any actual verification step.\" Technically accurate, but the handler comment documents the intended contract (frontend resolves first). The gap is that the backend has no `/bank/resolve` proxy endpoint and the frontend doesn't call one. The fix is smaller than the report implied — you don't need to redesign the flow, you need to add one endpoint and update the UI.\n\n---\n\n## Verified Priority List\n\nHere's what to actually build, in order, with honest scope estimates.\n\n---\n\n### Priority 0 — True Launch Blockers\n\n**1. Driver bank account + cashout**\n\nThis is the only thing that is genuinely broken end-to-end. Everything else is a gap or a risk. This is a hard failure.\n\nWhat's needed:\n- Migration: `driver_bank_accounts` table\n- Backend: `POST /driver/bank-account/verify` (proxies Paystack resolve), `POST /driver/bank-account`, `GET /driver/bank-account`\n- Backend: implement `ResolveCashoutRecipient` for drivers\n- API client: add driver bank account endpoints\n- Driver app: add bank account setup UI in the Earn tab\n\nEstimated effort: 2–3 days.\n\n**2. Bank account name server-side resolution (merchants + drivers)**\n\nThe backend needs to own the resolution call, not delegate it to the frontend. A malicious frontend can send any name.\n\nWhat's needed:\n- Add `ResolveAccount(ctx, bankCode, accountNumber string) (string, error)` to the Paystack provider\n- Add `POST /merchant/bank-account/resolve` endpoint that calls it and returns the name\n- Update `SaveBankAccount` to call resolve internally and ignore the client-supplied name\n- Update merchant UI to call resolve before showing the confirmation step\n\nEstimated effort: 1 day.\n\n**3. PIN brute-force protection**\n\nWhat's needed:\n- Migration: add `attempt_count int`, `locked_until timestamptz` to `pins` table\n- Update `VerifyPIN` to increment on failure, lock after 5, check lock before comparing\n- Add OTP-based unlock endpoint\n- Update `ConfirmByCard` to use the same lockout check\n\nEstimated effort: 1 day.\n\n**4. First boot downloads and processes Nigeria map (~2GB, ~20 min)\n4. Set `OSRM_URL` in production env to the Railway internal URL\n\nEstimated effort: 2 hours.\n\n**6. Build a single page with the numbers you need to run the business on day one.\n\nWhat's needed:\n- One backend endpoint: `GET /admin/metrics` returning today's order count, GMV, revenue, active drivers, active merchants, failed payments, cancellation count\n- One admin page that displays them\n\nEstimated effort: 1 day.\n\n**7. Leaked Sendbyte key**\n\nRotate the key immediately. Remove the duplicate line from `.env`. Add `QUOTE_SECRET`, `PAYCODE_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` to `.env`.\n\nEstimated effort: 30 minutes.\n\n---\n\n### Priority 2 — Before Public Marketing Push\n\n**8. Fraud velocity checks**\n\nThe rate limiter fails open on Redis errors (auth endpoints). Fix: pass a `failClosed bool` to `RateLimit`, set it true for `/auth` and `/otp` groups.\n\n**9. Driver bank account flow leaks sensitive banking data> \n> \nCurrent UI:> \n> \n```tsx> \n{bankAccount.bankName} · {bankAccount.accountNumber}> \n```> \n> \nYou should not show the full account number.> \n> \nChange:> \n> \n```tsx> \n{bankAccount.bankName} · ****{bankAccount.accountNumber.slice(-4)}> \n```> \n> \nReason:> \n> \n* If driver phone is compromised, attacker gets payout information.> \n* Standard fintech behaviour is masked account numbers.> \n> \n---> \n> \n## 3. Bank code input is too manual> \n> \nCurrent:> \n> \n```> \nBank code (e.g. 058 for GTBank)> \n```> \n> \nThis creates support issues.> \n> \nDrivers will enter:> \n> \n* GTBank> \n* Gt bank> \n* 58> \n* 058> \n* Guaranty Trust> \n> \nBetter:> \n> \nBackend endpoint:> \n> \n```> \nGET /banks> \n```> \n> \nReturns:> \n> \n```json> \n[> \n {> \n   \"code\":\"058\",> \n   \"name\":\"Guaranty Trust Bank\"> \n }> \n]> \n```> \n> \nFrontend:> \n> \nDropdown:> \n> \n```> \nSelect bank> \n↓> \nGTBank> \nAccess Bank> \nFirst Bank> \n...> \n```> \n> \nReason:> \n> \n* Removes human error.> \n* Paystack already provides bank lists.> \n> \n---> \n> \n## 4. Account verification needs rate limiting> \n> \nEndpoint:> \n> \n```> \nPOST /drivers/bank-account/resolve> \n```> \n> \nCurrently a driver can spam Paystack resolution.> \n> \nAdd:> \n> \n```> \n5 requests/minute/user> \n```> \n> \nReason:> \n> \n* Prevent Paystack API abuse.> \n* Reduce unnecessary costs.> \n> \n---> \n> \n## 5.
